drafts.proof_strategy: The difference of two decompositions lies in p ∩ q, and an element of p ∩ q has two decompositions.
sketch_steps: setup: Assume p ∩ q = 0 and p + q = M.
derive: Two decompositions satisfy y - y' = z' - z in p ∩ q, so they agree.
setup: Conversely assume unique decompositions.
derive: Existence gives p + q = M.
conclude: For x in p ∩ q the decompositions x + 0 and 0 + x coincide, so x = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a submodule p of a module M over a ring and the quotient M/p are both finitely generated, then M is finitely generated.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_submodule"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="quotient_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Lift generators of the quotient and add generators of the submodule.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose generators y_i of p and lifts x_j of generators of M/p.
derive: For x in M, subtract a combination of the x_j to land in p.
derive: Express the remainder through the y_i.
conclude: The x_j and y_i together generate M.

drafts.canonical_statement: For subgroups H and K of a finite group G, the product set HK = {hk} satisfies |HK|·|H∩K| = |H|·|K|, without assuming that HK is a subgroup.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_inter"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Count the fibres of the multiplication map from H × K onto HK.
sketch_steps: setup: Define φ from H × K onto HK by φ(h,k) = hk.
derive: hk = h₀k₀ holds exactly when h₀⁻¹h = k₀k⁻¹ lies in H ∩ K.
construct: The map t ↦ (h₀t, t⁻¹k₀) is a bijection from H ∩ K onto the fibre over h₀k₀.
conclude: All fibres have size |H ∩ K|, so |H||K| = |HK||H ∩ K|.

drafts.canonical_statement: If H and K are subgroups of finite index in a group G and the indices [G:H] and [G:K] are coprime, then [G:H∩K] = [G:H][G:K].
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_index_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_index_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="gcd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_inter"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Combine the upper bound from the coset pair map with divisibility from the tower law.
sketch_steps: derive: The map g(H∩K) ↦ (gH, gK) is injective, so [G:H∩K] ≤ [G:H][G:K].
apply_theorem: The tower law shows that [G:H] and [G:K] divide [G:H∩K].
derive: Coprimality makes the product [G:H][G:K] divide [G:H∩K].
conclude: The two bounds give equality.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a subgroup H of index 2 in a group G and elements a, b of G, ab lies in H if and only if a ∈ H is equivalent to b ∈ H.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_mul"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Pass to the quotient of order two and check the four cases.
sketch_steps: setup: H is normal and G/H has order 2, with non-identity element c.
translate: Membership in H means that the image in G/H is 1.
case_split: Compute π(a)π(b) in the four cases using c² = 1.
conclude: π(ab) = 1 exactly when π(a) = π(b).

drafts.canonical_statement: A subgroup H of prime index in a group G is maximal, that is, H ≠ G and any subgroup K with H ≤ K ≤ G equals H or G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the tower law to the prime index.
sketch_steps: setup: Let H ≤ K ≤ G with [G:H] = p prime.
apply_theorem: The tower law gives p = [G:K][K:H].
case_split: One of the two factors equals 1.
conclude: Hence K = G or K = H.

drafts.canonical_statement: For subgroups H, K, L of a group G with H ≤ L, the sets HK ∩ L and H(K ∩ L) coincide. No normality is assumed.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_inter"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Move the factor h across, using that H lies in L.
sketch_steps: setup: Write x = hk with h in H and k in K, and assume x lies in L.
derive: Since h lies in L, the element k = h⁻¹x also lies in L.
derive: Conversely hk lies in L when h is in H ≤ L and k is in K ∩ L.
conclude: The two sets coincide.

drafts.canonical_statement: If the conjugacy class of an element g of a group G is finite, its size equals the index [G:C_G(g)] of the centralizer of g.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="conjugacy_class"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="conjugacy_class"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="element_centralizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Identify conjugates of g with left cosets of its centralizer.
sketch_steps: setup: Consider xC_G(g) ↦ xgx⁻¹.
derive: xgx⁻¹ = ygy⁻¹ holds exactly when y⁻¹x lies in C_G(g).
conclude: The map is a bijection from the left cosets onto the conjugacy class.

drafts.canonical_statement: If the set of conjugates gHg⁻¹ of a subgroup H of a group G is finite, its size equals the index [G:N_G(H)] of the normalizer of H.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="conjugate_subgroups"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="conjugate_subgroups"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_index"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_normalizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Identify conjugates of H with left cosets of its normalizer.
sketch_steps: setup: Consider xN ↦ xHx⁻¹ where N is the normalizer of H.
derive: xHx⁻¹ = yHy⁻¹ holds exactly when y⁻¹x lies in N.
conclude: The map is a bijection, so the number of conjugates is [G:N].

drafts.canonical_statement: If a group G acts transitively on a set X and N is a normal subgroup of G, then any two N-orbits are in bijection; in particular all N-orbits have the same size.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="transitive_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="equinumerous"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_orbit"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_orbit"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Translate an orbit by an element of G and use normality.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose g with y = gx.
derive: g(nx) = (gng⁻¹)(gx) lies in Ny since N is normal.
derive: ny = g((g⁻¹ng)x) shows the reverse inclusion.
conclude: Multiplication by g is a bijection from Nx onto Ny.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a group G acts transitively on X, x is a point and H a subgroup, then H acts transitively on X if and only if every g in G can be written g = hs with h in H and s in Stab_G(x).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="transitive_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="transitive_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_stabilizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Translate transitivity of H into a factorization through the stabilizer of x.
sketch_steps: derive: If H is transitive, choose h with hx = gx; then h⁻¹g stabilizes x.
derive: If G = HS, any y = gx = hsx = hx lies in the orbit Hx.
conclude: X is a single H-orbit exactly when G = HS.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a group G acts transitively on a set X with at least two points and x is a point of X, the action is primitive (the only blocks are singletons and X) if and only if Stab_G(x) is a maximal subgroup of G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="transitive_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="primitive_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="action_stabilizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Set up an inclusion-preserving bijection between subgroups containing the stabilizer and blocks containing x.
sketch_steps: construct: Send K ⊇ S to the orbit Kx and a block B containing x to its setwise stabilizer.
derive: Kx is a block, and the setwise stabilizer of B contains S.
derive: The two assignments are mutually inverse and preserve inclusion.
translate: S corresponds to {x} and G corresponds to X.
conclude: Blocks through x are trivial exactly when S is maximal.

drafts.canonical_statement: If N is a normal subgroup of a finite group G and N is a p-group for a prime p, then N is contained in every Sylow p-subgroup of G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="p_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sylow_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Put N in one Sylow subgroup, then conjugate.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: N lies in some Sylow p-subgroup Q.
apply_theorem: Sylow subgroups are conjugate, so P = gQg⁻¹.
conclude: Normality gives N = gNg⁻¹ ≤ P.

drafts.canonical_statement: A normal subgroup of order 2 in a group G is contained in the center of G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_center"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Conjugation fixes the unique non-identity element of N.
sketch_steps: setup: Write N = {1, x}.
derive: gxg⁻¹ lies in N and is not 1, so it equals x.
conclude: x commutes with every g, so N lies in the center.

drafts.canonical_statement: Frattini argument. If N is a normal subgroup of a finite group G and P is a Sylow p-subgroup of N, then G = N·N_G(P).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sylow_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_normalizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Conjugate P by g inside N and correct by an element of N.
sketch_steps: setup: For g in G, gPg⁻¹ is again a Sylow p-subgroup of N.
apply_theorem: Sylow conjugacy in N gives n in N with gPg⁻¹ = nPn⁻¹.
derive: n⁻¹g normalizes P.
conclude: g = n(n⁻¹g) lies in N·N_G(P).

drafts.canonical_statement: A normal Sylow p-subgroup P of a finite group G is characteristic, that is, φ(P) = P for every automorphism φ of G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sylow_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_iso"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_image"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The image of P is a Sylow subgroup, hence conjugate to P, hence equal to P.
sketch_steps: derive: φ(P) has the same order as P, so it is a Sylow p-subgroup.
apply_theorem: Sylow conjugacy gives φ(P) = gPg⁻¹.
conclude: Normality gives φ(P) = P.

drafts.canonical_statement: For primes p < q, every group of order pq has a normal subgroup of order q.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="lt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Take a subgroup of order q and use the normality of subgroups of smallest prime index.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Cauchy gives a subgroup H of order q.
derive: H has index p, the smallest prime dividing |G|.
apply_theorem: A subgroup of smallest prime index is normal.

drafts.canonical_statement: If p < q are primes with q ≢ 1 modulo p, then every group of order pq is cyclic.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="lt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nat_mod"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclic_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show both Sylow subgroups are normal, then multiply commuting generators of coprime order.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Sylow counting gives n_p = 1, so the subgroup A of order p is normal.
apply_theorem: The subgroup B of order q has smallest prime index, so it is normal.
derive: A ∩ B = 1, so elements of A and B commute.
derive: Generators x, y have commuting coprime orders, so xy has order pq.
conclude: G is cyclic, generated by xy.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p and a natural number n, if a group of order p^n is simple, then n = 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: The nontrivial center forces G to be abelian, and a simple abelian p-group has order p.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: A nontrivial p-group has nontrivial center.
derive: Simplicity gives Z(G) = G, so G is abelian.
derive: G is cyclic, and n ≥ 2 would give a proper nontrivial subgroup.
conclude: Hence n = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: A group homomorphism f from G to H between finite groups of coprime orders is trivial, that is, f(g) = 1 for all g.

drafts.proof_strategy: The order of f(g) divides both group orders.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Lagrange shows that the order of f(g) divides |H|.
derive: f(g)^|G| = 1 shows that it divides |G|.
conclude: Coprimality forces order 1, so f(g) = 1.

sketch_steps: derive: (gN)^|N| = N, so the order of gN divides |N|.
apply_theorem: Lagrange in G/N shows that it divides [G:N].
conclude: Coprimality gives gN = N, so g lies in N.

drafts.canonical_statement: For finite groups G and H, the product G × H is cyclic if and only if G and H are both cyclic and |G| and |H| are coprime.

sketch_steps: derive: Projections of a generator generate G and H.
apply_theorem: The order of (a,b) is the lcm of the orders of a and b.
derive: The lcm equals |G||H| exactly when the orders are coprime.
conclude: Both implications follow by comparing with |G × H|.

sketch_steps: derive: n·f(1) = f(n·1) = 0.
construct: k ↦ kx kills nZ and induces a map from Z/n to A.
derive: Any f with f(1) = x satisfies f(k·1) = kx.
conclude: Existence and uniqueness hold.

drafts.canonical_statement: The automorphism group of a cyclic group G is isomorphic to the unit group (Z/n)^× where n = |G|, with n = 0 when G is infinite.

sketch_steps: setup: Write G = ⟨a⟩ and φ_k(a) = a^k.

derive: φ_k is invertible exactly when k is a unit modulo n.
conclude: k ↦ φ_k is an isomorphism from (Z/n)^× onto Aut(G).

derive: The kernel is nZ for some n ≥ 0.

setup: Otherwise let n be the smallest positive element of H.

conclude: Mutual divisibility gives uniqueness.

drafts.proof_strategy: Define F(n,g) = a(n)b(g) and use the compatibility condition.
sketch_steps: construct: Define F(n,g) = a(n)b(g).
derive: The compatibility condition makes F multiplicative.
conclude: (n,g) = (n,1)(1,g) gives uniqueness.

drafts.canonical_statement: If group homomorphisms π from G to H and s from H to G satisfy π∘s = id, then ker π ∩ s(H) = 1 and every g in G can be written g = nt with n in ker π and t in s(H).

drafts.proof_strategy: Use t = s(π(g)) as the section part of g.
sketch_steps: derive: If s(h) lies in ker π, then h = π(s(h)) = 1.
construct: Put t = s(π(g)) and n = gt⁻¹.
conclude: π(n) = 1, so g = nt is the required factorization.

drafts.canonical_statement: Schur–Zassenhaus theorem, existence part. If N is a normal subgroup of a finite group G with |N| and [G:N] coprime, then N has a complement, a subgroup H with N ∩ H = 1 and NH = G.

drafts.proof_strategy: Treat abelian N by an averaging argument on transversals, and reduce the general case by the Frattini argument.
sketch_steps: setup: Induct on |G|, with m = [G:N].
construct: For abelian N, define the difference d(S,T) of transversals and the quotient set X.
derive: d(nS,S) = n^m, so N acts simply transitively on X; a stabilizer in G is a complement.
apply_theorem: For general N, the Frattini argument gives G = N·N_G(P) for a Sylow subgroup P of N.
induction: Apply the hypothesis to L/Z(P) to get K with |K| = |Z|m.
conclude: The abelian case in K yields H of order m, which complements N.

drafts.canonical_statement: If subgroups H_0, H_1, ... of a group G satisfy H_0 = G, H_n = 1 for some n, and [H_i,H_i] ≤ H_{i+1} for all i, then G is solvable.

name="seq_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare the derived series with the given chain by induction.
sketch_steps: setup: Let G^(i) be the derived series.
induction: G^(i) ≤ H_i for all i.
conclude: G^(n) ≤ H_n = 1, so G is solvable.

drafts.canonical_statement: A minimal normal subgroup N of a solvable group G, that is, a nontrivial normal subgroup containing no normal subgroups of G other than 1 and N, is abelian.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_mul"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_mul"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The commutator of N is normal in G, so it is 1 or N; the second case contradicts solvability.
sketch_steps: derive: [N,N] is normal in G and contained in N.
case_split: Minimality gives [N,N] = 1 or [N,N] = N.
induction: If [N,N] = N, then N lies in every derived subgroup of G.
contradiction: Solvability would force N = 1.
conclude: So [N,N] = 1 and N is abelian.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nonabelian simple group G satisfies [G,G] = G and Z(G) = 1.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="abelian_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="commutator_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_center"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Both subgroups are normal, and the abelian alternatives are excluded.
sketch_steps: derive: [G,G] and Z(G) are normal, so each is 1 or G.
contradiction: [G,G] = 1 or Z(G) = G would make G abelian.
conclude: Hence [G,G] = G and Z(G) = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: Burnside's normal p-complement theorem. If a Sylow p-subgroup P of a finite group G satisfies N_G(P) ≤ C_G(P), then there is a normal subgroup K of G with K ∩ P = 1 and KP = G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sylow_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_normalizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_centralizer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_inter"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Construct the transfer to P and show it restricts to the power map x ↦ x^m on P.
sketch_steps: derive: P is abelian because P ≤ N_G(P) ≤ C_G(P).
construct: Define the transfer V from G to P using coset representatives.
derive: On each ⟨x⟩-orbit, the contribution t⁻¹x^f t equals x^f by Sylow conjugacy in the centralizer.
derive: Hence V(x) = x^m for x in P, a bijection of P.
conclude: K = ker V is a normal complement of P.

drafts.canonical_statement: A finite group whose order is squarefree is solvable.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="squarefree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use Burnside's theorem at the smallest prime and induct on the order.
sketch_steps: setup: Induct on |G|; let p be the smallest prime factor and P a Sylow p-subgroup.
derive: N_G(P)/C_G(P) embeds in Aut(P), of order p-1, and its prime factors are at least p, so it is trivial.
apply_theorem: Burnside gives a normal complement K of P.
induction: K is solvable, and G/K is abelian.
conclude: G is solvable.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every maximal subgroup of a nilpotent group G is normal.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The normalizer grows, and maximality forces it to be G.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: In a nilpotent group a proper subgroup is properly contained in its normalizer.
conclude: Maximality gives N_G(H) = G, so H is normal.

drafts.canonical_statement: With lower central series γ_0 = G, γ_{i+1} = [γ_i,G] and upper central series Z_0 = 1, Z_{i+1} = {x : [x,y] ∈ Z_i for all y}, for each natural number n one has γ_n = 1 if and only if Z_n = G.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="lower_central_term"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="upper_central_term"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare the two series term by term in opposite directions by induction.
sketch_steps: induction: If γ_n = 1, then γ_(n-i) ≤ Z_i for all i ≤ n.
derive: Taking i = n gives Z_n = G.
induction: If Z_n = G, then γ_i ≤ Z_(n-i) for all i ≤ n.
conclude: Taking i = n gives γ_n = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nontrivial normal subgroup N of a nilpotent group G meets the center nontrivially, that is, N ∩ Z(G) ≠ 1.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="subgroup_inter"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_center"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="trivial_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show that N meets every term of the upper central series trivially.
sketch_steps: setup: Assume N ∩ Z(G) = 1 and use the upper central series.
induction: x in N ∩ Z_(i+1) has [x,y] in N ∩ Z_i = 1, so x is central.
conclude: Z_n = G gives N = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finite group G, the Frattini subgroup Φ(G), the intersection of all maximal subgroups, is nilpotent.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="frattini_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the Frattini argument to Sylow subgroups of Φ(G) and use that Φ(G) lies in every maximal subgroup.
sketch_steps: derive: Φ(G) is normal in G.
apply_theorem: The Frattini argument gives G = Φ(G)·N_G(P) for a Sylow subgroup P of Φ(G).
contradiction: If N_G(P) were proper, a maximal subgroup containing it would contain G.
apply_theorem: All Sylow subgroups of Φ(G) are normal, so Φ(G) is nilpotent.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a normal subgroup N of a group G, the quotient G/N is simple if and only if N ≠ G and the only normal subgroups containing N are N and G. This characterizes each step of a composition series.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="quotient_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_subgroup"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="or"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Transport normal subgroups along the correspondence theorem.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The correspondence theorem matches normal subgroups of G containing N with normal subgroups of G/N.
translate: N corresponds to 1 and G corresponds to G/N.
conclude: Simplicity of G/N is the stated maximality.

drafts.canonical_statement: If l_1, ..., l_r are the lengths of the cycles of length at least 2 in the disjoint cycle decomposition of a permutation σ of a finite set, then sgn(σ) = (-1)^(l_1+...+l_r+r).

drafts.proof_strategy: Multiply the signs of the disjoint cycles.
sketch_steps: setup: Decompose σ into disjoint cycles of lengths l_i.
apply_theorem: A cycle of length l has sign (-1)^(l+1).
conclude: The sign homomorphism gives the product formula.

drafts.canonical_statement: The only surjective homomorphism from the symmetric group of a finite set onto {±1} is the sign map.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="group_hom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="symmetric_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sign_group"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="surjective_function"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sign_homomorphism"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Transpositions are conjugate and generate, so s is determined by its common value on them.
sketch_steps: derive: s is constant on transpositions because they are conjugate and the target is abelian.
contradiction: Value 1 would make s trivial, since transpositions generate.
conclude: s and sgn agree on the generators.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a permutation of a finite set is written in two ways as a product of pairwise disjoint cycles (excluding the identity), the two expressions agree up to the order of the factors.

drafts.proof_strategy: Each cycle is recovered from σ as σ restricted to one orbit.
sketch_steps: setup: Let σ be the common product and c a factor moving x.
derive: On its support c agrees with σ, and its support is the σ-orbit of x.
derive: The factor of the other list moving x has the same description.
conclude: Hence the two lists contain the same cycles.

drafts.canonical_statement: The center of the symmetric group on a finite set with at least 3 elements is trivial.

drafts.proof_strategy: A nonidentity permutation fails to commute with a suitable transposition.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose σ(a) ≠ a and pick c outside {a, σ(a)}.
construct: Let τ be the transposition of σ(a) and c.
contradiction: στ(a) = σ(a) but τσ(a) = c.
conclude: Hence σ is the identity.

drafts.proof_strategy: Intersect with the simple group Alt(X) and exclude the trivial intersection using the center.
sketch_steps: derive: N ∩ A is 1 or A since A is simple.
contradiction: N ∩ A = 1 would give a central subgroup of order 2.
derive: So A ≤ N, and [S:A] = 2.
conclude: N equals A or S.

sketch_steps: construct: Send a word to the corresponding product of f(a)^(±1) in G.
derive: Removing aa⁻¹ does not change the value, so the map is well defined on classes.
derive: Concatenation goes to products, so it is a homomorphism.
conclude: Generators determine a homomorphism, which gives uniqueness.

drafts.proof_strategy: Contract a maximal subtree of the Cayley tree whose vertices lie in distinct H-orbits, so that H acts simply transitively on the vertices of a new tree.
sketch_steps: setup: The Cayley graph T of F is a tree, and H acts freely on its vertices and preserves edge orientation.
construct: Zorn gives a maximal subtree Y whose vertices lie in distinct H-orbits; its translates partition the vertices of T.
construct: Contracting the translates gives a directed graph T′ with vertex set H.
derive: Lifting reduced paths back to T shows that T′ is a tree.
derive: The edges of T′ are h → hs for s in a set S with S ∩ S⁻¹ empty.
conclude: Reduced words in S give reduced paths in T′, so S is a free basis of H.

drafts.proof_strategy: Map the generator to 1 and check bijectivity on powers of a.
sketch_steps: construct: a ↦ 1 respects the relator, giving φ from P to Z/n.
derive: Every element of P is a power a^k, and φ(a^k) = k mod n.
derive: φ(a^k) = 0 forces n | k, hence a^k = 1.
conclude: φ is bijective.

sketch_steps: setup: Take a generating set S and a right transversal R containing 1.
construct: Let H′ be generated by u(r,s) = rs·(rs̄)⁻¹.
derive: H′R is closed under right multiplication by S and S⁻¹, so H′R = G.
derive: For h in H, its representative is 1, so h lies in H′.
conclude: H = H′ has at most [G:H]|S| generators.

derive: Any product of more than mr commutators can be shortened.
conclude: [G,G] consists of bounded products of finitely many elements.

drafts.canonical_statement: If A → B → C → 0 is an exact sequence of modules over a ring with maps f and g, then for every module X the sequence 0 → Hom(C,X) → Hom(B,X) → Hom(A,X) is exact; that is, u∘g = 0 implies u = 0, and v∘f = 0 implies v = u∘g for some u.

derive: v∘f = 0 gives ker g = im f ⊆ ker v.
construct: Define u(g(b)) = v(b), which is well defined and linear.
conclude: u∘g = v.

derive: g_2(b(y)) = 0, so b(y) = g_1(z) with z = a(w).
derive: Injectivity of b gives y = f_1(w).
conclude: Exactness at A_2 gives x = 0.

sketch_steps: setup: Order partial extensions of f by extension.
apply_theorem: Zorn gives a maximal extension (C,h).
construct: For b outside C, I = {r : rb in C} and g(r) = h(rb) extend to R, giving q.
contradiction: k(c+rb) = h(c)+rq is a proper extension.
conclude: C = B.

drafts.proof_strategy: Embed M in its double character dual and then in a product of copies of D(R).
sketch_steps: setup: D(X) = Hom_Z(X, Q/Z), with Q/Z divisible.
derive: Characters separate points, so M → D(D(M)) is injective.
derive: D(R) is an injective R-module, and products of injectives are injective.
construct: A surjection from a free right module onto the right module D(M) dualizes to an injection into D(R)^J.
conclude: The composite embeds M into an injective module.

drafts.canonical_statement: A module M over a commutative ring R is flat if and only if for every ideal I the map I ⊗ M → R ⊗ M is injective.

conclude: Tensoring with M preserves all injections.

drafts.canonical_statement: A module M over a principal ideal domain R is flat if and only if it is torsion-free, meaning that r ≠ 0 and rm = 0 imply m = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use multiplication by r in one direction and the ideal criterion for principal ideals in the other.
sketch_steps: derive: Flatness preserves the injection r from R to R, so M is torsion-free.
setup: For the converse, an ideal is I = (a).
derive: I ⊗ M → M identifies with multiplication by a.
apply_theorem: The ideal criterion gives flatness.

drafts.canonical_statement: For modules M, N, P over a commutative ring R there is a linear isomorphism Hom(M ⊗ N, P) ≅ Hom(M, Hom(N, P)) sending f to m ↦ (n ↦ f(m ⊗ n)).

drafts.proof_strategy: Identify both sides with bilinear maps through the universal property.
sketch_steps: construct: Define e(f)(m)(n) = f(m ⊗ n).
derive: Pure tensors generate, so e is injective.
apply_theorem: The universal property turns h into f with f(m ⊗ n) = h(m)(n).
conclude: e is a linear isomorphism.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring R and an R-module M, (R/I) ⊗ M ≅ M/IM.

drafts.proof_strategy: Tensor the presentation of R/I with M and use right exactness.
sketch_steps: setup: Start from the exact sequence I → R → R/I → 0.
apply_theorem: Right exactness of the tensor product applies.
translate: Under R ⊗ M ≅ M the image of I ⊗ M is IM.
conclude: Hence (R/I) ⊗ M ≅ M/IM.

drafts.canonical_statement: For ideals I and J of a commutative ring R, (R/I) ⊗ (R/J) ≅ R/(I+J).

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the formula (R/I) ⊗ M ≅ M/IM with M = R/J.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: (R/I) ⊗ (R/J) ≅ (R/J)/I(R/J).
derive: I(R/J) = (I+J)/J.
apply_theorem: The third isomorphism theorem gives R/(I+J).

drafts.proof_strategy: Multiply a pure tensor by 1 = ua + vb.
sketch_steps: derive: m ⊗ n = u(am ⊗ n) + v(m ⊗ bn).
derive: Both terms vanish by the annihilator conditions.
conclude: Pure tensors generate, so the tensor product is 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: If M is a torsion module and N is a divisible module over a domain R, then M ⊗ N = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Move the annihilating scalar across the tensor sign.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose r ≠ 0 with rm = 0 and n′ with n = rn′.
derive: m ⊗ n = rm ⊗ n′ = 0.
conclude: Pure tensors generate.

drafts.canonical_statement: A submodule N of a module M with a finite basis indexed by ι over a principal ideal domain R has a basis with n ≤ |ι| elements.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the rank by projecting to the last coordinate and using that the image ideal is principal.
sketch_steps: setup: Induct on k, with π the last coordinate and N′ = N ∩ ker π.
derive: π(N) = (a) because R is a PID.
case_split: If a = 0, then N = N′.
construct: If a ≠ 0, choose x in N with π(x) = a; then N = Rx ⊕ N′.
conclude: Adding x to a basis of N′ gives a basis of N.

drafts.canonical_statement: A finitely generated module M without torsion over a principal ideal domain R is free.

drafts.proof_strategy: Embed M in a free module by a common denominator.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose a maximal independent subset of the generators and let F be its span.
derive: There is a ≠ 0 with aM ⊆ F.
derive: m ↦ am is injective because M is torsion-free.
apply_theorem: Submodules of free modules over a PID are free.

sketch_steps: derive: M/T is finitely generated and torsion-free, hence free.
apply_theorem: The surjection onto the projective M/T splits.
conclude: M = T ⊕ s(M/T), with the second factor free.

drafts.proof_strategy: Split off the torsion subgroup, which is finite, and apply the structure theorem for finite abelian groups.
sketch_steps: translate: G/T is a finitely generated torsion-free Z-module, so it is free of some rank n.
derive: The surjection onto the free module G/T splits, so G ≅ Z^n ⊕ T.
derive: T is finitely generated and torsion, so it is finite.
apply_theorem: The structure theorem for finite abelian groups decomposes T.

drafts.canonical_statement: For submodules N ≤ O of a module with a finite basis over a principal ideal domain R, there are a basis (e_1,...,e_o) of O, a basis (f_1,...,f_n) of N with n ≤ o, and a_i in R with f_i = a_i e_i. Divisibility among the a_i is not claimed.

drafts.proof_strategy: Choose a functional maximizing the image ideal of N and split off one basis vector.
sketch_steps: setup: Induct on the rank of O; choose φ_0 with φ_0(N) = (a) maximal.
derive: For every functional ψ and y in N with φ_0(y) = a, a divides ψ(y).
construct: Write y = ax, so φ_0(x) = 1 and O = Rx ⊕ ker φ_0.
derive: N = Ry ⊕ (N ∩ ker φ_0).
induction: Apply the hypothesis to ker φ_0 and adjoin x, y.

drafts.proof_strategy: The annihilator of m also annihilates f(m).
sketch_steps: setup: Choose r ≠ 0 with rm = 0.
derive: rf(m) = f(rm) = 0.
conclude: Torsion-freeness gives f(m) = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: A module M over a ring R is simple if and only if M ≅ R/I for a maximal left ideal I of R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the map r ↦ rx and the correspondence theorem.
sketch_steps: construct: For x ≠ 0, r ↦ rx is a surjection from R onto M with kernel I.
apply_theorem: The correspondence theorem matches submodules of R/I with left ideals containing I.
conclude: M is simple exactly when I is maximal.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a submodule N of a module M over a ring R, the quotient M/N is simple if and only if N is a maximal submodule of M.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the correspondence theorem.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Submodules of M/N correspond to submodules between N and M.
translate: 0 corresponds to N and M/N to M.
conclude: Simplicity of M/N is maximality of N.

drafts.canonical_statement: Submodules and quotient modules of a semisimple module M over a ring R (every submodule has a complement) are semisimple.

drafts.proof_strategy: Intersect a complement with N, and identify the quotient with a complement.
sketch_steps: derive: For N′ ≤ N with M = N′ ⊕ C, the modular law gives N = N′ ⊕ (C ∩ N).
derive: With M = N ⊕ C_0 one has M/N ≅ C_0.
conclude: Both are semisimple.

drafts.canonical_statement: A semisimple module M over a ring R is a direct sum of simple submodules; there is an independent family of simple submodules whose sum is M.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="semisimple_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="submodule_family"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="independent_submodule_family"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="submodule_family_sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="whole_submodule"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Take a maximal independent family of simple submodules by Zorn.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: M is the sum of its simple submodules.
apply_theorem: Zorn gives a maximal independent family S.
derive: A simple submodule outside ΣS meets it in 0, contradicting maximality.
conclude: ΣS = M.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a semisimple module M over a ring R, being finitely generated, Noetherian and Artinian are equivalent.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="semisimple_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="artinian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show each condition is equivalent to the index set of a simple decomposition being finite.
sketch_steps: setup: Write M as a direct sum of simple modules over an index set J.
derive: Finite generation forces J to be finite.
derive: Infinite J gives strictly increasing and decreasing chains.
derive: Finite J gives both chain conditions by closure under extensions.
conclude: All conditions are equivalent to the finiteness of J.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every module over a semisimple ring R (R is semisimple as a left module over itself) is both projective and injective.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="semisimple_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="projective_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="injective_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: All modules are semisimple, so the relevant maps split.
sketch_steps: derive: Every module is a quotient of a direct sum of copies of R, hence semisimple.
construct: For a surjection g, a complement of ker g gives a section.
construct: For an injection i, a complement of i(X) gives an extension.
conclude: M is projective and injective.

drafts.proof_strategy: Transport ascending chains to M.
sketch_steps: derive: Chains in N are chains in M.
derive: Chains in M/N pull back to chains in M.
conclude: U_i = π(π⁻¹(U_i)) gives stabilization.

derive: Chains in M/N pull back to chains in M.
conclude: U_i = π(π⁻¹(U_i)) gives stabilization.

drafts.canonical_statement: If M → N → P is exact at N for modules over a ring R, and M and P are Artinian, then N is Artinian.
