drafts.proof_strategy: Control a chain in N by its preimage in M and image in P.
sketch_steps: derive: A ≤ B with the same preimage and the same image must be equal.
setup: Take a descending chain (N_i).
derive: Its preimages in M and images in P stabilize.
conclude: The chain (N_i) stabilizes.

drafts.canonical_statement: A finitely generated module over a left Noetherian ring R is a Noetherian module.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: R^n is Noetherian by extensions, and M is a quotient of R^n.
sketch_steps: induction: R^n is Noetherian by closure under extensions.
construct: Generators give a surjection from R^n onto M.
conclude: Quotients of Noetherian modules are Noetherian.

drafts.canonical_statement: A module M over a ring R has finite length (a composition series from 0 to M) if and only if it is both Noetherian and Artinian.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_length_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="artinian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use closure under extensions for one direction and build a series from maximal submodules for the other.
sketch_steps: induction: A composition series gives both chain conditions.
construct: Noetherianity gives a maximal proper submodule at each step.
derive: Artinianity makes the descending chain reach 0.
conclude: This chain is a composition series.

drafts.canonical_statement: Jordan–Hölder theorem for modules. Two composition series from 0 to M of a module over a ring R are equivalent; they have the same length and isomorphic simple factors up to permutation.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="composition_series"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="composition_series"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="equivalent_composition_series"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the length, comparing the two maximal submodules through their intersection.
sketch_steps: setup: Let A and B be the penultimate terms of the two series.
case_split: If A = B, apply induction to A.
derive: If A ≠ B, then A + B = M and M/A ≅ B/C, M/B ≅ A/C with C = A ∩ B.
construct: Intersecting the series with C gives a composition series of C.
induction: Compare both series through the series of C.
conclude: Lengths agree and factors match up to permutation.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a short exact sequence 0 → N → M → P → 0 over a ring R, lengths with values in N ∪ {∞} satisfy ℓ(M) = ℓ(N) + ℓ(P).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_hom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_hom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="injective_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="surjective_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="exact_pair"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_length"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_length"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_length"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Concatenate composition series, and treat infinite length through the chain conditions.
sketch_steps: construct: f(N_i) followed by g⁻¹(P_j) is a composition series of M.
apply_theorem: Jordan–Hölder gives ℓ(M) = a + b.
contradiction: If M had finite length, so would N and P.
conclude: Otherwise both sides are infinite.

drafts.canonical_statement: Fitting's lemma. For an endomorphism f of a module M over a commutative ring that is both Noetherian and Artinian, there is n > 0 with M = ker f^n ⊕ im f^n. This generalizes Fitting's lemma for finite-dimensional vector spaces to modules of finite length.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="artinian_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_hom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="lt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="complementary_submodules"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="map_kernel"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="map_power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="map_image"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="map_power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Choose n where both chains have stabilized.
sketch_steps: derive: ker f^i and im f^i stabilize for large i.
derive: ker f^n ∩ im f^n = 0 because ker f^(2n) = ker f^n.
derive: im f^n = im f^(2n) gives the sum decomposition.

name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="or"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Fitting's lemma and indecomposability.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Fitting gives M = ker f^n ⊕ im f^n with n > 0.
case_split: One of the summands is 0.
conclude: im f^n = 0 gives nilpotence, and ker f^n = 0 gives bijectivity.

drafts.canonical_statement: For modules X and Y over a ring R, the natural map from Hom_R(X,Y) to Ext^0_R(X,Y) is bijective.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="bijective_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_of_hom_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compute Ext⁰ from a projective resolution and use left exactness of Hom.
sketch_steps: setup: Ext⁰ is the kernel of d* on Hom(P_0,Y).
apply_theorem: Left exactness identifies this kernel with Hom(X,Y).

drafts.canonical_statement: For a projective module P over a ring R, a module Y and a natural number n, Ext^(n+1)_R(P,Y) = 0.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="projective_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="is_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="zero_module"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: P is its own projective resolution.
sketch_steps: setup: P has the projective resolution 0 → P → P → 0.
conclude: The Hom complex vanishes in positive degree.

drafts.proof_strategy: Y is its own projective resolution.
sketch_steps: setup: Tor is computed from a projective resolution of Y.
derive: Y itself is a resolution, with zero terms in positive degree.
conclude: The homology vanishes in degree n + 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: A rational number q is integral over the integers if and only if q is an integer.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_integer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Z"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Clear denominators in a monic integer relation and use coprimality of numerator and denominator.
sketch_steps: setup: Write q = a/b in lowest terms with a monic integer relation.
derive: Multiplying by b^n shows that b divides a^n.
derive: Coprimality forces b = 1.
conclude: Conversely an integer n is a root of X - n.

drafts.canonical_statement: An element x of a number field is an algebraic integer if and only if all coefficients of its minimal polynomial over Q are integers.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_integer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_coeff"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Z"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The forward direction factors a monic integer polynomial and applies Gauss's lemma.
sketch_steps: setup: Let f be the minimal polynomial and g a monic integer polynomial killing x.
derive: Write g = f h with f and h monic rational polynomials.
apply_theorem: Gauss's lemma applied to primitive multiples of f and h forces integer coefficients.
conclude: Conversely f itself is a monic integer relation.

drafts.canonical_statement: For every element x of a number field there is a nonzero integer d such that dx is an algebraic integer.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Z"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_integer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Multiply a monic rational relation by a power of a common denominator.
sketch_steps: setup: Take a monic rational relation for x.
construct: Let d be a common denominator of the coefficients.
derive: Multiplying by d^n gives a monic integer relation for dx.

drafts.canonical_statement: The norm and the trace from a number field to Q of an algebraic integer are integers.

drafts.proof_strategy: Express norm and trace through conjugates, which are algebraic integers, and use that rational algebraic integers are integers.
sketch_steps: translate: Write norm and trace as a product and a sum over complex embeddings.
derive: Each conjugate is a root of the same monic integer polynomial.
derive: Algebraic integers are closed under sums and products.
conclude: A rational algebraic integer is an integer.

drafts.canonical_statement: Kronecker's theorem. If x is an algebraic integer of a number field and |φ(x)| = 1 for every complex embedding φ, then x^n = 1 for some positive integer n.

drafts.proof_strategy: The powers of x lie in a finite set of algebraic integers with bounded conjugates, so two of them coincide.
sketch_steps: setup: All powers of x are algebraic integers whose conjugates have modulus one.
apply_theorem: Only finitely many algebraic integers of K have all conjugates bounded by one.
derive: Hence x^k = x^l for some k < l.
conclude: Since x is nonzero, x^(l-k) = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a number field K and a real number B, only finitely many algebraic integers x of K satisfy |φ(x)| ≤ B for every complex embedding φ.

drafts.proof_strategy: The characteristic polynomials have bounded integer coefficients, so there are finitely many of them and finitely many roots.
sketch_steps: construct: Attach to x the polynomial g_x, the product of X - φ(x) over all embeddings.
derive: g_x has integer coefficients because it is a power of the minimal polynomial.
derive: The coefficients are bounded in terms of n and B.
conclude: Finitely many polynomials have finitely many roots, and one embedding is injective.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nonzero algebraic integer x of a number field has a complex embedding σ with |σ(x)| ≥ 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: The product of the absolute values of the conjugates is a nonzero integer in absolute value.
sketch_steps: translate: The norm is the product of the conjugates and is a nonzero integer.
contradiction: If all conjugates had modulus below one, the product would too.

drafts.proof_strategy: Write multiplication by x as a block matrix with commuting blocks in a product basis.
sketch_steps: setup: Use the product basis a_i b_j of L over K.
translate: Multiplication by x becomes a block matrix built from the regular representation of F.
derive: Summing diagonal blocks gives transitivity of the trace.
apply_theorem: The determinant formula for commuting blocks gives transitivity of the norm.

drafts.proof_strategy: Identify the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by x with the product of X - σ(x), then compare coefficients.
sketch_steps: setup: Let f be the minimal polynomial and m the degree of K over Q(x).
derive: The characteristic polynomial of multiplication by x is f^m.
derive: Each root of f has m embeddings above it, so the product of X - σ(x) is also f^m.
conclude: Compare the constant coefficient and the coefficient of X^(n-1).

drafts.canonical_statement: If the powers 1, α, ..., α^(n-1) form a Q-basis of a number field K and f = X^n + c_(n-1) X^(n-1) + ... + c_0 is the minimal polynomial of α, then N(α) = (-1)^n c_0 and Tr(α) = -c_(n-1).

drafts.proof_strategy: Multiplication by α in the power basis is the companion matrix of f.
sketch_steps: translate: Write multiplication by α in the power basis.
derive: The matrix is the companion matrix of f, whose characteristic polynomial is f.
conclude: Read off the determinant and the trace from the coefficients.

drafts.canonical_statement: If an element x of a number field satisfies Tr_{K/Q}(xy) = 0 for all y in K, then x = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Test the hypothesis on the inverse of x, using that the trace of 1 is the degree.
sketch_steps: contradiction: Suppose x is nonzero and take y to be its inverse.
derive: The trace of 1 is the degree of K, which is nonzero.
conclude: This contradicts the hypothesis, so x = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: An element x of the ring of integers of a number field divides the integer N_{K/Q}(x) in the ring of integers.

drafts.proof_strategy: The quotient of the norm by x is the product of the other conjugates, hence integral.
sketch_steps: case_split: The case x = 0 is immediate.
construct: Let y be the norm divided by x, an element of K.
derive: Under one embedding y becomes the product of the remaining conjugates, an algebraic integer.
conclude: Injectivity of the embedding shows y is integral, so x divides the norm.

drafts.canonical_statement: Any two Z-bases b, b' of the ring of integers of a number field have the same discriminant det(Tr(b_i b_j)), and this value is nonzero.

drafts.proof_strategy: A change of integral basis has determinant ±1, and nondegeneracy of the trace form gives nonvanishing.
sketch_steps: setup: The two bases differ by an integer matrix A with determinant ±1.
derive: The trace matrices satisfy T' = A T A^t, so the determinants agree.
contradiction: A vanishing determinant would give a nonzero x orthogonal to K under the trace form.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finite field extension L/F, a finite family b of elements of L and a square matrix P over F, the family b'_i = sum_j P_ij b_j satisfies disc(b') = det(P)^2 disc(b), where disc(b) = det(Tr(b_i b_j)).

drafts.proof_strategy: The trace matrix transforms as a bilinear form under the change of family.
sketch_steps: derive: Bilinearity of the trace gives T' = P T P^t.
conclude: Taking determinants gives the factor det(P)^2.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a number field K, a finite family b indexed by I and a bijection i ↦ σ_i from I to the complex embeddings of K, the discriminant det(Tr(b_i b_j)) equals det(σ_j(b_i))^2.

drafts.proof_strategy: The matrix of embeddings times its transpose is the trace matrix.
sketch_steps: construct: Let M be the matrix of values σ_j(b_i).
derive: The trace is the sum over embeddings, so M M^t is the trace matrix.
conclude: Take determinants.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compute the discriminant with Vandermonde and rewrite the product of differences as the norm of f'(α).
sketch_steps: translate: The discriminant is the squared Vandermonde determinant of the conjugates.
derive: f'(α_i) is the product of α_i - α_j over j different from i.
derive: Multiplying over i and pairing factors produces the sign.
conclude: Compare the two expressions.

drafts.canonical_statement: If θ is an algebraic integer whose powers below the degree form a Q-basis of a number field K, and d is the discriminant of this basis, then dz lies in Z[θ] for every algebraic integer z of K.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_integer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="power_basis_generator"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="extension_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_integer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="family_discriminant"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="power_family"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integer_adjoin"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Solve for the coordinates of z with the integer trace matrix and Cramer's rule.
sketch_steps: setup: Write z in the power basis with rational coordinates.
translate: Taking traces of z θ^i gives a linear system with integer data and determinant d.
apply_theorem: Cramer's rule shows d times each coordinate is an integer.
conclude: Hence dz lies in Z[θ].

drafts.canonical_statement: The sign of the discriminant d_K of a number field K is (-1)^(r_2), where r_2 is the number of complex places.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sign_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="absolute_discriminant"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="unary_minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="complex_places_count"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Complex conjugation permutes the columns of the embedding matrix by r_2 transpositions.
sketch_steps: setup: Write d_K as the square of the determinant of the embedding matrix.
derive: Conjugation swaps r_2 pairs of columns, so the conjugate determinant has sign (-1)^(r_2).
case_split: The determinant is real or purely imaginary according to the parity of r_2.
conclude: Squaring gives the sign.

drafts.canonical_statement: A number field K of degree n with r_2 complex places satisfies |d_K| ≥ n^(2n) / ((4/π)^(2 r_2) (n!)^2).

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the Minkowski bound for a nonzero integer and use that its norm is at least one in absolute value.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The Minkowski bound gives a nonzero integer with small norm.
derive: The absolute value of the norm of a nonzero integer is at least 1.
conclude: Rearrange and square.

drafts.canonical_statement: A number field K of degree at least 2 has |d_K| > 2.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="extension_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="gt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="abs"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="absolute_discriminant"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Bound the Minkowski expression below by a sequence increasing in n and evaluate it at n = 2.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Start from the Minkowski lower bound for |d_K|.
derive: Since 2 r_2 ≤ n, it dominates a_n = (π/4)^n n^(2n)/(n!)^2.
induction: The ratio a_(n+1)/a_n is at least π, so a_n grows.
conclude: a_2 = π²/4 is larger than 2.

drafts.canonical_statement: Dedekind's discriminant theorem. For a number field K and a prime p, p does not divide d_K if and only if every prime ideal of the ring of integers containing p is unramified over Z.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dvd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="absolute_discriminant"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ring_of_integers"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_number_in_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ramified_prime"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce the discriminant modulo p to the trace form of O_K/pO_K and analyze this algebra by its nilpotents.
sketch_steps: translate: The reduction of d_K mod p is the discriminant of the trace form of A = O_K/pO_K.
derive: The factorization of p gives A as a product of local pieces.
case_split: A ramified prime yields a nilpotent in the radical of the trace form.
case_split: If nothing ramifies, A is a product of finite fields with nondegenerate trace forms.

drafts.canonical_statement: Minkowski's ramification theorem. If K is a number field of degree different from 1, then some maximal ideal of the ring of integers is ramified over Z.

drafts.proof_strategy: The discriminant has absolute value above 1, so a prime divides it, and that prime ramifies.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The lower bound gives |d_K| > 2.
derive: Hence a prime p divides d_K.
apply_theorem: Dedekind's theorem yields a ramified prime ideal over p.
conclude: Nonzero primes of the ring of integers are maximal.

drafts.canonical_statement: The ring of integers of a number field K of degree n is a free Z-module of rank n, that is, it has a Z-basis with n elements.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_basis"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="extension_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Sandwich the ring of integers between a lattice spanned by a basis of integers and the lattice of its trace dual.
sketch_steps: construct: Choose a Q-basis of K consisting of algebraic integers.
derive: The trace dual basis exists since the trace form is nondegenerate.
derive: Integrality of traces places O_K inside the dual lattice.
apply_theorem: Subgroups of free abelian groups of rank n are free of rank at most n.

drafts.proof_strategy: Squares are 0 or 1 modulo 4, according to parity.
sketch_steps: setup: Squares modulo 4 are 0 for even numbers and 1 for odd numbers.
case_split: If d is 2 or 3 mod 4, an odd B makes A^2 a nonsquare mod 4.
case_split: If d is 1 mod 4, then A^2 and B^2 agree mod 4.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let K be a quadratic number field, d a squarefree integer and s in K with s^2 = d, s not rational, and a, b rational. If d is 2 or 3 mod 4, then a + b s is integral iff a, b are integers. If d is 1 mod 4, then a + b s is integral iff a = m/2, b = n/2 for integers m, n of the same parity.

sketch_steps: translate: x is integral iff its trace 2a and norm a² - d b² are integers.
derive: Squarefreeness of d forces 2b to be an integer.
derive: With A = 2a and B = 2b the condition is 4 | A² - d B².
case_split: Solve this congruence for d congruent to 2, 3 or 1 modulo 4.

drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce by the Chinese remainder theorem to prime powers and count along the chain of powers of a prime.
sketch_steps: setup: Factor ideals into prime powers.
apply_theorem: The Chinese remainder theorem reduces to one prime power.
derive: Each quotient p^i/p^(i+1) is one-dimensional over the residue field.
conclude: Multiplying along the chain gives N(p^a) = N(p)^a, hence multiplicativity.

drafts.proof_strategy: The ideal (x) is the image of the lattice under the integer matrix of multiplication by x, whose determinant is the norm.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a Z-basis of O_K.
translate: Multiplication by x has an integer matrix A with determinant N(x).
apply_theorem: The index of A Z^n in Z^n is |det A|.

drafts.canonical_statement: If the norm of an element x of the ring of integers of a number field is a prime number up to sign, then x is a prime element.

drafts.proof_strategy: The quotient by (x) has prime order, hence is a field.
sketch_steps: translate: The index of (x) equals |N(x)| = p.
derive: A unital ring of prime order is Z/pZ.
conclude: Hence (x) is a nonzero prime ideal and x is a prime element.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a number field K and a natural number n, the ring of integers has only finitely many nonzero ideals of norm at most n.

drafts.proof_strategy: An ideal of index m contains m, and only finitely many ideals contain m.
sketch_steps: derive: An ideal of index m contains m by Lagrange.
derive: The ring O_K/mO_K is finite, so finitely many ideals contain m.
conclude: Take the union over m from 1 to n.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers of a number field there are a prime number p contained in it and a positive integer n such that its index is p^n.

drafts.proof_strategy: The residue ring is a finite field, whose order is a power of its characteristic.
sketch_steps: derive: The quotient is a finite integral domain, hence a finite field.
construct: Let p be its characteristic, so p lies in the ideal.
conclude: A finite field of characteristic p has order p^n with n positive.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an extension L/K of number fields and an ideal I of O_K, the relative norm of the extended ideal I O_L is I^[L:K], where the relative norm of an ideal J of O_L is the ideal of O_K generated by the norms of elements of J.

drafts.proof_strategy: Check the equality after localizing at each maximal ideal, where the extended ideal is generated by a power of a uniformizer.
sketch_steps: case_split: The zero ideal is immediate.
translate: Two ideals of O_K agree if they agree after localizing at every maximal ideal p.
setup: In the discrete valuation ring A = (O_K)_p write IA = (π^k), so the localized extended ideal is π^k B.
derive: The localized norm ideal is generated by norms of elements of π^k B.
derive: Each such norm is π^(kn) times an element of A, and π^k itself has norm π^(kn).
conclude: Hence the norm ideal localizes to I^n A for every p.

sketch_steps: derive: Localizing at p makes O_L free of rank n, so the quotient has dimension n.
apply_theorem: The Chinese remainder theorem splits the quotient along the primes above p.
derive: Each factor has dimension e_i f_i by the chain of powers.
conclude: Add the dimensions.

sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Start from the fundamental identity.
derive: Each e and f is at least 1, so the number of terms is at most the degree.
conclude: Each single term bounds its e and f.

sketch_steps: setup: Factor p in O_F and then P in O_L, isolating P and Q.
derive: The cofactor of P stays prime to Q because Q contracts to P.
derive: Hence the exponent of Q in pO_L is e e'.
conclude: The residue fields form a tower, which gives the formula for f.

drafts.proof_strategy: Separate Q from all conjugates of P by the Chinese remainder theorem and take the norm.
sketch_steps: case_split: Dispose of the zero ideal, so that all primes involved are maximal.
contradiction: If Q is no conjugate of P, choose x in Q outside every conjugate of P.
derive: The norm of x lies in Q ∩ O_K = p, which is contained in P.
conclude: Primality of P puts some σ(x) in P, a contradiction.

drafts.proof_strategy: The Galois group acts transitively on the primes above p and preserves e and f, so all terms of the fundamental identity agree.
sketch_steps: derive: Automorphisms fix pO_L and hence preserve exponents and residue degrees.
apply_theorem: Transitivity shows e and f are independent of the prime above p.
conclude: The fundamental identity becomes g e f = [L:K].

drafts.canonical_statement: Kummer–Dedekind. Let θ be in the ring of integers of a number field and p a prime not dividing the least positive d with d O_K in Z[θ] (or 0 if none). The primes above p correspond bijectively to the monic irreducible factors of the minimal polynomial f of θ mod p; the factor g mod p corresponds to the prime (p, g(θ)), whose inertia degree is deg g mod p and whose ramification index is the multiplicity of g mod p in f mod p.

sketch_steps: derive: p not dividing d gives O_K/pO_K isomorphic to F_p[X]/(f mod p).
translate: Maximal ideals correspond to irreducible factors, with residue degree the degree of the factor.
derive: The relation f(θ) = 0 bounds the true exponents by the multiplicities.
apply_theorem: The fundamental identity forces equality.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let p be a prime, k ≥ 0, p not dividing m, n = p^(k+1) m and K the n-th cyclotomic extension of Q. Every prime P of O_K above p has ramification index p^k (p-1) and inertia degree the multiplicative order of p modulo m.

drafts.proof_strategy: Split the extension into the unramified layer Q(ζ_m) and the totally ramified layer obtained from an Eisenstein polynomial.
sketch_steps: setup: Let F be the m-th cyclotomic subfield.
apply_theorem: Kummer–Dedekind shows p is unramified in F with residue degree the order of p mod m.
derive: Φ_(p^(k+1))(X+1) is Eisenstein at primes of F above p, so K/F is totally ramified there.
conclude: Multiply e and f along the tower.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let p be a prime, k ≥ 0, K the p^(k+1)-th cyclotomic extension of Q and ζ a primitive p^(k+1)-th root of unity. As ideals of O_K, (p) = (ζ - 1)^[K:Q], and there is exactly one prime above p.

drafts.proof_strategy: Factor p as the product of 1 - ζ^j, show all factors are associates of 1 - ζ, and use the fundamental identity.
sketch_steps: derive: Evaluating the cyclotomic polynomial at 1 gives p as a product of 1 - ζ^j.
derive: Each 1 - ζ^j is an associate of 1 - ζ.
translate: Hence (p) = (ζ - 1)^n with n = [K:Q].
apply_theorem: The fundamental identity forces (ζ - 1) to be prime and unique above p.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an odd prime p, let K be the p-th cyclotomic extension of Q and ζ a primitive p-th root of unity. The basis (ζ-1)^i, 0 ≤ i ≤ p-2, of K has discriminant (-1)^((p-1)/2) p^(p-2).

drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce to the basis of powers of ζ and compute the norm of Φ_p'(ζ) by differentiating (X-1)Φ_p(X) = X^p - 1.
sketch_steps: derive: The change of basis to powers of ζ - 1 has determinant 1.
apply_theorem: The discriminant of a power basis is ± the norm of Φ_p'(ζ).
derive: Differentiation gives (ζ-1)Φ_p'(ζ) = pζ^(p-1).
conclude: Compute the norms and determine the sign.

sketch_steps: derive: The product of Φ_d(1) over divisors d > 1 of n equals n.
derive: Prime power divisors already contribute n, so the others have product 1.
derive: Hence Φ_n(1) = ±1.
conclude: 1 - ζ divides Φ_n(1) in the ring of integers.

drafts.proof_strategy: The Minkowski bound is below 2, so every ideal class contains the unit ideal.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Every class contains an ideal of norm at most the Minkowski bound M.
derive: If M < 2 the class group is trivial.
derive: Compute M for the two fields from n, r_2 and the discriminant.
conclude: Both values are below 2.

sketch_steps: setup: Write a unit as a + bζ using that Z[ζ] is the ring of integers.

case_split: Completing the square leaves six integer solutions.
conclude: Identify them with ±ζ^j.

drafts.proof_strategy: Blichfeldt's pigeonhole argument applied to s/2 produces two points differing by a lattice element, and convexity places it in s.
sketch_steps: setup: Let t = s/2, whose measure exceeds that of F.
derive: The translates of t by L cannot be disjoint inside F.
construct: So x - l = y - l' for distinct lattice points, giving w = y - x in L.
conclude: Symmetry and convexity place w in s.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the convex body theorem to the sum-norm ball in the Minkowski space and use the AM-GM inequality.
sketch_steps: setup: Embed I as a lattice with covolume 2^(-r_2) sqrt|d_K| N(I).
construct: Use the convex symmetric sets S_t with known volume.
apply_theorem: The convex body theorem and a compactness limit give a nonzero point in S_(t_0).
conclude: AM-GM bounds the norm by (t_0/n)^n.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every ideal class of a number field K of degree n with r_2 complex places contains a nonzero ideal I of the ring of integers with N(I) ≤ (4/π)^(r_2) n!/n^n sqrt(|d_K|).

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the Minkowski estimate to an ideal in the inverse class and divide.
sketch_steps: construct: Pick an ideal J in the inverse class.
apply_theorem: Find a nonzero a in J with |N(a)| ≤ N(J) M.
derive: Write (a) = J I, so I lies in the class C.
conclude: Multiplicativity of the norm gives N(I) ≤ M.

conclude: The converse divides by x.

drafts.canonical_statement: If h is the class number of a number field K, then I^h is principal for every nonzero ideal I of the ring of integers.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ring_of_integers"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_is_principal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="class_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Lagrange's theorem in the class group.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: In a finite group of order h, every element has h-th power 1.
derive: The class of I^h is the h-th power of the class of I.
conclude: A trivial class means a principal ideal.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let h be the class number of a number field K. If I is a nonzero ideal of the ring of integers, m is coprime to h and I^m is principal, then I is principal.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ring_of_integers"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="gcd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="class_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_is_principal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_is_principal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The order of the class of I divides both m and h, hence equals 1.
sketch_steps: derive: The class of I has m-th power 1 and h-th power 1.
derive: Its order divides gcd(m, h) = 1.
conclude: The class is trivial, so I is principal.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a number field K of degree n with r_2 complex places satisfies |d_K| < (2 (π/4)^(r_2) n^n/n!)^2, then its ring of integers is a principal ideal domain.

drafts.proof_strategy: The hypothesis says the Minkowski bound is below 2, so every class contains the unit ideal.
sketch_steps: translate: The hypothesis is equivalent to the Minkowski bound M being below 2.
apply_theorem: Each class contains an ideal of norm at most M.
conclude: Such an ideal is the unit ideal, so the class group is trivial.

drafts.canonical_statement: Dirichlet's unit theorem. For a number field K with r_1 real and r_2 complex places, the Z-rank r of the unit group of the ring of integers satisfies r + 1 = r_1 + r_2.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_group_rank"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="real_places_count"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="complex_places_count"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The logarithmic embedding gives a lattice in the trace-zero hyperplane; Minkowski's theorem produces enough units.
sketch_steps: construct: Define the logarithmic embedding into the hyperplane of sum zero.
derive: Bounded sets contain finitely many images, so the image is discrete and the rank is at most r_1 + r_2 - 1.
apply_theorem: Minkowski's theorem yields elements of bounded norm with shrinking absolute values.
derive: Their ratios are units negative at all places but one.
conclude: Diagonal dominance shows these units span the hyperplane.

drafts.canonical_statement: Existence of a fundamental system. If a number field K has r+1 infinite places, there are units u_1, ..., u_r such that every unit x is uniquely of the form ζ times the product of the u_i^(e_i), with ζ a root of unity in the units and e_i integers.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fundamental_unit_family"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unique_torsion_exponents"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Choose lifts of a Z-basis of the free quotient of the unit group by its torsion.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The unit group is finitely generated of rank r with torsion μ.
derive: The quotient by μ is free of rank r.
construct: Lift a basis of the quotient to units u_i.
conclude: Coordinates in the quotient determine the e_i, and then ζ.

drafts.canonical_statement: A unit u of the ring of integers of a number field is a root of unity if and only if |φ(u)| = 1 for every complex embedding φ.

drafts.proof_strategy: One direction is immediate; the other is Kronecker's theorem.
sketch_steps: derive: A root of unity has conjugates of modulus one.
apply_theorem: Kronecker's theorem gives the converse.

drafts.canonical_statement: The torsion subgroup of the unit group of a number field, that is, the group of roots of unity of K, is finite and cyclic.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="torsion_units"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclic_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="torsion_units"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Finiteness comes from bounded conjugates, cyclicity from counting roots of X^d - 1 in a field.
sketch_steps: derive: Roots of unity are algebraic integers with conjugates of modulus one.
apply_theorem: Only finitely many such elements exist.
conclude: A finite subgroup of the multiplicative group of a field is cyclic.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a unit u of a number field, the sum over the infinite places w of m_w log|u|_w is 0, where m_w is 1 for real and 2 for complex places.

drafts.proof_strategy: The product of the absolute values with multiplicities is the absolute norm of u, which is 1.
sketch_steps: translate: The product of |u|_w^(m_w) over places is |N(u)|.
derive: The norm of a unit is ±1.
conclude: Take logarithms.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let w be the number of roots of unity of a number field K. If P is a nonzero prime ideal with N(P) coprime to w, then w divides N(P) - 1.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ring_of_integers"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="gcd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="torsion_order"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dvd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="torsion_order"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Roots of unity inject into the residue field units when the norm is coprime to w.
sketch_steps: construct: Reduce roots of unity modulo the prime.
contradiction: A nontrivial kernel element of order m would put m in the prime, contradicting coprimality.
apply_theorem: Lagrange in the multiplicative group of the residue field gives the divisibility.

drafts.canonical_statement: The unit group of a quadratic number field without real places, an imaginary quadratic field, is finite.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="number_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="extension_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="real_places_count"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: A unit has norm ±1, and in an imaginary quadratic field the norm is the squared modulus, so all conjugates of a unit have modulus one.
sketch_steps: setup: The two embeddings are complex conjugates of each other.
derive: The norm of a unit is ±1 and equals |σ(u)|^2, so |σ(u)| = 1.
apply_theorem: Only finitely many algebraic integers of K have all conjugates bounded by 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: A quadratic number field without complex places, a real quadratic field, has a unit of infinite order.

drafts.proof_strategy: The unit rank is 1, so not all units can have finite order.
sketch_steps: derive: r_2 = 0 and degree 2 give r_1 = 2.
apply_theorem: Dirichlet's theorem gives rank 1.
contradiction: If all units were torsion, the rank would be 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: For n > 2, the unit rank r of the n-th cyclotomic extension K of Q satisfies 2(r + 1) = φ(n).

drafts.proof_strategy: Primitive roots of unity of order above 2 are not real, so K is totally complex; apply Dirichlet's theorem.
sketch_steps: derive: Images of ζ are nonreal for n > 2, so r_1 = 0.
derive: The degree φ(n) equals 2 r_2.
apply_theorem: Dirichlet's theorem gives r + 1 = r_2.

drafts.canonical_statement: A number field K with r_1 real and r_2 complex places satisfies r_1 + 2 r_2 = [K:Q].

drafts.proof_strategy: Count the complex embeddings according to the action of complex conjugation.
sketch_steps: setup: K has exactly n complex embeddings.
derive: Complex conjugation fixes real embeddings and pairs the others.
conclude: Counting gives r_1 + 2 r_2 = n.

drafts.canonical_statement: For x in a number field K, the product over the infinite places w of |x|_w^(m_w) equals |N_{K/Q}(x)|, where m_w is 1 for real and 2 for complex places.

drafts.proof_strategy: Group the factors of the norm by infinite place.
sketch_steps: translate: Write |N(x)| as the product of |σ(x)| over embeddings.
derive: Each place contributes m_w embeddings with the same absolute value.
conclude: Regroup the product.

drafts.canonical_statement: The product formula. For a nonzero x in a number field, the values |x|_v = N(p_v)^(-ord(x)) at finite places differ from 1 only finitely often, and the product of |x|_w^(m_w) over infinite places times the product of |x|_v over finite places is 1.

sketch_steps: derive: The factorization of (x) has finite support.
derive: Multiplicativity of ideal norms gives the finite product |N(x)|^(-1).
derive: The infinite product is |N(x)|.
conclude: Multiply.

drafts.canonical_statement: An element x of a number field K is an algebraic integer if and only if its valuation at every nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers is nonnegative, that is, its multiplicative value is at most 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compare with the prime factorization of the fractional ideal (x).
sketch_steps: translate: The exponents of (x) are the valuations of x.
derive: An integral ideal has nonnegative exponents.
conclude: Conversely nonnegative exponents make (x) an integral ideal.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a Galois extension L/K of number fields and a nonzero prime Q of O_L, with q the size of the residue ring of O_K at the contraction of Q, there is σ in Gal(L/K) with σ(x) - x^q in Q for every x in O_L.

drafts.proof_strategy: Lift a generator of the residue field to an element avoiding the other conjugates of Q and use its characteristic polynomial.
sketch_steps: construct: Choose y lifting a generator of the residue field and lying in every other conjugate of Q.
derive: The polynomial over O_K with roots τ(y) has a^q as a root modulo Q, so a^q ≡ σ(y).
derive: Since a^q is nonzero, σ fixes Q.
conclude: Powers of y give the congruence for all x.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let L/K be a Galois extension of number fields, Q a nonzero prime of O_L, q the residue ring size below Q and σ a Frobenius element at Q. If ζ in O_L satisfies ζ^m = 1 and m is not in Q, then σ(ζ) = ζ^q.

drafts.proof_strategy: Two distinct m-th roots of unity cannot coincide modulo Q when m is not in Q, since X^m - 1 is then separable modulo Q.
sketch_steps: setup: σ(ζ) and ζ^q are m-th roots of unity congruent modulo Q.
contradiction: If they differ, X^m - 1 has a double root modulo Q.
derive: The derivative test then forces m to lie in Q.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a number field K, the residue value 2^(r_1) (2π)^(r_2) R h / (w sqrt|d_K|) of the Dedekind zeta function at s = 1 is positive, with R the regulator, h the class number and w the number of roots of unity.

sketch_steps: derive: Powers of 2 and 2π, h, w and sqrt|d_K| are positive.
apply_theorem: The log vectors of a fundamental system are linearly independent, so R > 0.
conclude: A quotient of positive numbers is positive.

sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The number of ideals of norm at most x is asymptotic to κ x.
derive: Abel summation writes ζ_K(s) as s times an integral of A(x) x^(-s-1).
derive: The integral over a bounded range is negligible after multiplying by s - 1.
conclude: The tail is controlled by κ ± ε.

drafts.canonical_statement: Weber's theorem. If A(s) counts the ideals of the ring of integers of a number field with norm at most s, where the zero ideal has norm 0, then A(s)/s tends to 2^(r_1) (2π)^(r_2) R h / (w sqrt|d_K|) as s tends to infinity.

drafts.proof_strategy: Count ideals class by class as lattice points in a dilated fundamental cone of the unit action.
sketch_steps: translate: Ideals in a class correspond to elements of a lattice modulo units.
construct: Use a fundamental cone for the action of units.
apply_theorem: Lattice point counting in a dilate of a Lipschitz domain gives the volume ratio.
derive: Compute the volume of the cone and the covolume of the lattice.
conclude: Sum over the h classes.

drafts.canonical_statement: A finite adele a = (a_v) of a number field K is a unit if and only if a_v is nonzero for every finite place v and |a_v|_v = 1 for all but finitely many v.

drafts.proof_strategy: Inverses are componentwise, and the restricted product condition is equivalent to almost all values being 1.
sketch_steps: derive: If a has inverse b, almost all components of both are integral, so |a_v| = 1 for those v.
construct: Conversely define b componentwise by inverses.
conclude: The condition makes b a finite adele.

sketch_steps: derive: The product of completions has real dimension n.
derive: Nonvanishing of the discriminant shows a Q-basis of K gives an R-basis.
conclude: Density of Q^n in R^n transfers along the linear homeomorphism.

derive: Compactness of the maximal ideal gives a largest value below 1.
conclude: A generator of the maximal ideal makes the ring a discrete valuation ring.

derive: If p divides v, then p does not divide u, so the valuation is negative.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p, the natural numbers are dense in Z_p.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dense_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_integers"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Approximate x by a rational with denominator prime to p and invert the denominator modulo p^n.
sketch_steps: derive: Approximate x by a rational r = u/v with p not dividing v.
construct: Choose a natural number a congruent to u times an inverse of v modulo p^n.
conclude: The ultrametric inequality gives |x - a|_p ≤ p^(-n).

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p, the ring Z_p is compact and complete.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_integers"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="complete_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_integers"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: A closed subset of a complete space is complete; residues modulo p^n form finite nets.
sketch_steps: derive: Z_p is closed in the complete space Q_p.
construct: The integers from 0 to p^n - 1 form a finite ε-net.
conclude: A complete totally bounded metric space is compact.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p, every closed ball of Q_p is compact, but Q_p itself is not compact.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="R"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="closed_ball"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="compact_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Closed balls sit inside scaled translates of the compact set Z_p, and Q_p is unbounded.
sketch_steps: derive: A closed ball is closed in a translate of p^(-k) Z_p.
apply_theorem: Z_p is compact and scaling is a homeomorphism.
contradiction: The norms of p^(-n) are unbounded, so Q_p is not compact.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p and a sequence a_n in Q_p, the series of a_n is unconditionally summable if and only if a_n tends to 0.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_sequence"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="summable_sequence_qp"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_tends_to"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: In an ultrametric complete space, the Cauchy criterion for finite sums reduces to the size of single terms.
sketch_steps: derive: Summable series have terms tending to 0.
derive: The ultrametric inequality bounds finite tail sums by the largest term.
apply_theorem: Completeness of Q_p gives convergence of the Cauchy net.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p and x in Q_p with |x|_p < 1, the series of x^n over n ≥ 0 converges in Q_p to (1 - x)^(-1).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="lt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_norm"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="has_sum_fn"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The terms tend to 0, and the telescoping identity identifies the limit.
sketch_steps: derive: The norm of x^n tends to 0, so the series is summable.
derive: Partial sums equal (1 - x^n)/(1 - x).
conclude: Let n tend to infinity.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p and a sequence x_n in Q_p, if x_(n+1) - x_n tends to 0, then x_n converges in Q_p.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_sequence"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="indexed_tends_to"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="padic_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="seq_tends_to"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Telescoping and the ultrametric inequality turn the hypothesis into the Cauchy condition.
sketch_steps: derive: Write x_m - x_n as a telescoping sum of consecutive differences.
derive: The ultrametric inequality bounds it by the largest difference.
apply_theorem: Completeness of Q_p gives the limit.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p, x, y in Q_p and real r, if y lies in the open ball B(x, r), then B(x, r) = B(y, r), and B(x, r) is both open and closed.
