drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on m and simplify the ratio of consecutive factorials.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on m, with both sides equal to 1 at m = 0.
derive: The new factor is C(N, n-1) n! (m+1) with N = mn + n - 1.
derive: Expand the binomial coefficient and use n(m+1) = N + 1.
conclude: The factor equals ((m+1)n)!/(mn)!.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let D_n be the number of derangements, that is fixed-point-free permutations, of an n-element set. Then D_{n+2} = (n+1)(D_n + D_{n+1}).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="derangement_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="derangement_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="derangement_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Fix the image b of an element a and split on whether b maps back to a.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a and the image b = σ(a), which has n+1 choices.
case_split: Consider σ(b) = a and σ(b) ≠ a.
construct: In the first case σ restricts to a derangement of the remaining n elements.
construct: In the second case rerouting through b gives a derangement of n+1 elements, bijectively.
conclude: Add the two counts and multiply by n+1.

drafts.canonical_statement: The number D_n of derangements of an n-element set satisfies D_{n+1} = (n+1) D_n - (-1)^n as integers.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="derangement_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="derangement_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="unary_minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on n and substitute the inductive hypothesis into the two-term recurrence.
sketch_steps: setup: Recall D_{n+2} = (n+1)(D_n + D_{n+1}).
induction: The case n = 0 follows from D_0 = 1 and D_1 = 0.
derive: Replace (n+1) D_n with D_{n+1} + (-1)^n.
conclude: This gives the identity for n+1.

drafts.canonical_statement: With D_k the number of derangements of a k-element set, sum_{k=0}^n C(n,k) D_k = n!.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integer_range"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="binom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="derangement_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="factorial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Classify permutations by the set of non-fixed points.
sketch_steps: setup: Associate to a permutation its set Y of non-fixed points.
derive: The permutation restricts to a derangement of Y.
construct: A subset Y and a derangement of Y extend uniquely to a permutation fixing the complement.
conclude: Counting by the size of Y gives the identity.

drafts.canonical_statement: With D_n the number of derangements of an n-element set, D_n/n! tends to e^(-1) as n tends to infinity.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="tends_to_at_top"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="derangement_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="factorial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="transc1" name="exp"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="unary_minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Divide the inclusion-exclusion formula by n! and recognize a partial sum of the exponential series at -1.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Inclusion-exclusion gives D_n as an alternating sum.
derive: Dividing by n! gives the sum of (-1)^k/k! for k ≤ n.
conclude: This is a partial sum of the series for e^(-1), so it converges there.

drafts.canonical_statement: Among the permutations of an n-element set, the number of cycles of length k, with 2 ≤ k ≤ n and all other points fixed, is (k-1)! C(n,k); in particular there are (n-1)! full cycles.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="perm_of_cycle_type"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="factorial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="binom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Choose the support and count cyclic orderings of it.
sketch_steps: setup: A cycle is determined by its support and a cyclic order.
derive: There are C(n,k) supports.
derive: Each of the k! orderings gives a cycle, with exactly k orderings per cycle.
conclude: Multiply to get (k-1)! C(n,k).

drafts.canonical_statement: Let c(m) be the number of permutations of an n-element set whose cycles of length at least 2 have the multiset of lengths m. If all elements of m are at least 2 and their sum s is at most n, then c(m) (n-s)! (product of m) (product over i of m_i!) = n!, where m_i is the multiplicity of i in m.

drafts.proof_strategy: Count sequences of all elements that read off a permutation of the given cycle type.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix an order of m and consider all n! sequences of the elements.
construct: Cut the sequence into blocks of the lengths in m and read the blocks as cycles.
derive: Each permutation of cycle type m arises.
derive: The number of sequences per permutation is (n-s)! times the product of m times the product of m_i!.
conclude: Double counting gives the identity.

drafts.canonical_statement: Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality. If a family of subsets of an n-element set is an antichain under inclusion and a_r is the number of its members of size r, then the sum of a_r / C(n,r) over r from 0 to n is at most 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: Count pairs consisting of an ordering of X and a member of the antichain that is a prefix of the ordering.
sketch_steps: setup: Consider all n! orderings of X and their prefixes.
derive: A set of size r is a prefix of exactly r!(n-r)! orderings.
derive: Prefixes of one ordering form a chain, so at most one member of the antichain occurs.
conclude: Double counting and division by n! give the inequality.

drafts.canonical_statement: Local LYM inequality. For a family A of r-element subsets of an n-element set with shadow ∂A, one has |A| r ≤ |∂A| (n - r + 1).

drafts.proof_strategy: Double count the pairs (S, T) with S in A and T obtained from S by removing an element.
sketch_steps: setup: Count the pairs (S, T) with S in A, T in the shadow and T contained in S.
derive: Each S contributes exactly r pairs.
derive: Each T has at most n - r + 1 extensions to an r-set.
conclude: Comparing the two counts gives the inequality.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compress A repeatedly with UV-compressions, which do not enlarge the shadow, until it becomes the initial segment.
sketch_steps: setup: Reduce to |C| = |A| by passing to a subfamily of A.
construct: Define UV-compression, which preserves the size of a family.
derive: If the family is compressed for the smaller pairs (U - u, V - v), then the shadow of the UV-compression lies in the UV-compression of the shadow.
derive: A family compressed for all pairs with max U < max V is an initial segment.
derive: Compressing along a non-compressed pair with |U| minimal keeps the shadow from growing and strictly decreases the binary weight, so the process stops.
conclude: The final family equals C, so the shadow of C is at most that of A.

drafts.canonical_statement: Lovász form of Kruskal-Katona. If i ≤ r ≤ k ≤ n and A is a family of r-subsets of {0,...,n-1} with |A| ≥ C(k,r), then the i-th iterated shadow satisfies |∂^i A| ≥ C(k, r-i).

drafts.proof_strategy: Compare A with the family of all r-subsets of {0,...,k-1} and iterate Kruskal-Katona.
sketch_steps: construct: Let C_j be the family of all (r-j)-subsets of the first k elements, an initial segment of colex.
derive: The shadow of C_j is C_{j+1}.
induction: Kruskal-Katona applied to C_j and the j-th shadow of A gives |C_{j+1}| ≤ |∂^{j+1} A|.
conclude: For j = i this is C(k, r-i) ≤ |∂^i A|.

drafts.canonical_statement: Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem. If 1 ≤ r, 2r ≤ n and A is a family of r-subsets of {0,...,n-1} in which any two members have a common element, then |A| ≤ C(n-1, r-1).

drafts.proof_strategy: Use Katona's cycle method and count arcs in cyclic orders.
sketch_steps: setup: Consider cyclic arrangements of X and arcs of r consecutive elements.
derive: At most r arcs of one arrangement belong to A, because 2r ≤ n makes opposite arcs at a cut disjoint.
derive: Each r-set is an arc in r!(n-r)! arrangements.
conclude: Double counting gives |A| ≤ C(n-1, r-1).

drafts.canonical_statement: Pajor's lemma. A finite family A of finite sets shatters at least |A| sets, where A shatters s when every subset of s has the form s ∩ S with S in A.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="shatterer"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the ground set by splitting the family at an element.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on the size of the union of the members.
construct: Split A at an element a into A_0 and A_1 with a removed.
derive: Sets shattered by A_0 or A_1 are shattered by A.
derive: For s shattered by both, s with a added is also shattered by A.
conclude: Inclusion-exclusion gives at least |A_0| + |A_1| shattered sets.

drafts.canonical_statement: Sauer-Shelah lemma. If a family A of subsets of an n-element set has VC dimension d, the largest size of a shattered set and 0 for the empty family, then |A| ≤ sum_{k=0}^d C(n,k).

drafts.proof_strategy: Combine Pajor's lemma with a count of subsets of size at most d.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Pajor's lemma bounds |A| by the number of shattered sets.
derive: Every shattered set is a subset of X of size at most d.
conclude: The number of such subsets is the sum of C(n,k) for k ≤ d.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a family A shatters s, then it shatters every subset t of s.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="shatters"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="shatters"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Intersect the witness for a subset of t with the smaller set t.
sketch_steps: setup: Take u contained in t, so u is contained in s.
derive: There is S in A with s ∩ S = u.
conclude: Then t ∩ S = t ∩ u = u.

drafts.canonical_statement: If any two members, possibly equal, of a family A of subsets of an n-element set have a common element, then 2|A| ≤ 2^n.

drafts.proof_strategy: A member and its complement are disjoint, so the family has at most one set from each complementary pair.
sketch_steps: setup: Pair each subset with its complement.
derive: The family contains at most one set from each pair.
case_split: For n = 0 the family is empty.
conclude: Otherwise there are 2^(n-1) pairs.

drafts.canonical_statement: If any two members, possibly equal, of a family A of subsets of a nonempty n-element set have a common element, then A is contained in a family B with the same property and 2|B| = 2^n.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take a maximal intersecting family and show it contains exactly one set of each complementary pair.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose a maximal intersecting family B containing A.
case_split: If S is not in B, treat S empty and S nonempty.
derive: The complement of S meets every member of B, so it belongs to B.
derive: Exactly one set of each complementary pair lies in B.
conclude: Since n ≥ 1, the family has 2^(n-1) members.

drafts.canonical_statement: A family of subsets of a finite set X that is maximal among families in which any two members, possibly equal, have a common element is closed under supersets.

drafts.proof_strategy: Show that adding a superset keeps the intersecting property and apply maximality.
sketch_steps: setup: Take S in A and a superset T.
derive: T meets every member of A because S does, and T is nonempty.
conclude: Maximality forces T to belong to A.

drafts.proof_strategy: Extend each family to a maximal one and apply Harris-Kleitman to the complementary lower sets.
sketch_steps: setup: Extend each family to a maximal intersecting family of size 2^(n-1), which is upward closed.
derive: The complements are lower sets of size 2^(n-1).
apply_theorem: Harris-Kleitman gives a lower bound for intersections of lower sets.
induction: The intersection of k complements has at least 2^(n-k) members.
conclude: Taking complements gives the bound for the union.

drafts.canonical_statement: Harris-Kleitman inequality. If families A and B of subsets of an n-element set are both closed under taking subsets, then |A||B| ≤ 2^n |A ∩ B|.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the ground set by splitting at an element and use a Chebyshev-type product inequality.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on n, with n = 0 checked directly.
construct: Split both families at an element a.
derive: The lower-set property gives A_1 ⊆ A_0 and B_1 ⊆ B_0.
derive: The inductive hypothesis bounds both parts of the intersection.
conclude: The nonnegative product of the differences gives the final inequality.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a family A of subsets of an n-element set is closed under supersets and B is closed under subsets, then 2^n |A ∩ B| ≤ |A||B|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="powerset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="powerset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="upper_family"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="lower_family"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Harris-Kleitman to the complement of A and B, then rearrange.
sketch_steps: translate: The complement of the upper family A is a lower family.
apply_theorem: Apply Harris-Kleitman to the complement of A and B.
derive: Expand the sizes of the complement and of its intersection with B.
conclude: Rearrangement gives the inequality.

drafts.canonical_statement: Daykin inequality. For finite families A, B of finite sets, |A||B| ≤ |A ∧ B||A ∨ B|, where A ∧ B and A ∨ B consist of the intersections and the unions of members.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="family_meets"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="family_joins"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Prove the four functions theorem by induction on the ground set and apply it to the indicator functions of the four families.
sketch_steps: setup: Work in the Boolean lattice of a finite set containing all members.
induction: Reduce the four functions theorem from X to X minus a point by summing each function over the two extensions.
derive: The one-point step is the inequality obtained from (t - p)(t - q) ≥ 0.
construct: Take the indicators of A, B, the meets and the joins, which satisfy the pointwise hypothesis.
conclude: The four functions theorem on the whole lattice gives the inequality.

drafts.canonical_statement: Marica-Schönheim inequality, assuming the Daykin inequality. For a finite family A of finite sets, the family of differences S \ T with S, T in A has at least |A| members.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="family_differences"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the Daykin inequality to the family and the complements of its members.
sketch_steps: construct: Let B be the family of complements of members of A.
derive: The meets of A and B are exactly the differences.
derive: The joins of A and B are the complements of the differences.
apply_theorem: Daykin gives |A|^2 ≤ |D|^2.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a subset s of an n-element set X, the number of bijections f from X onto {0,...,n-1} with s = {a in X | f(a) < |s|} is |s|! (n-|s|)!.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="numberings_with_prefix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="factorial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="factorial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Split a valid bijection into its restrictions to s and to the complement of s.
sketch_steps: translate: The condition says f maps s onto {0,...,r-1} and the complement onto the rest.
construct: Such f correspond to pairs of bijections on the two parts.
conclude: The number of pairs is r!(n-r)!.

drafts.canonical_statement: For finite sets s and t of natural numbers, the sum of 2^i over s is less than the sum of 2^i over t if and only if s < t in colexicographic order, that is s ≠ t and the maximum of the symmetric difference lies in t.

drafts.proof_strategy: Cancel the common part and compare the top element of the symmetric difference with a geometric sum.
sketch_steps: derive: The common elements cancel from both sums.
derive: If the maximum m of the symmetric difference lies in t, the rest of s contributes at most 2^m - 1.
contradiction: For the converse, the opposite position of m would reverse the inequality.
conclude: The two orders coincide.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finite family A of finite sets and an element a, the down-compression D_a(A), consisting of S in A with S \ {a} in A and of S \ {a} for S in A with S \ {a} not in A, satisfies |D_a(A)| = |A|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="down_compression"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Construct an explicit bijection from A onto its compression.
sketch_steps: construct: Send S to itself when S \ {a} is in A and to S \ {a} otherwise.
derive: The map is surjective by the definition of the compression.
case_split: Check injectivity for each pair of cases.
conclude: The map is a bijection, so sizes are equal.

drafts.canonical_statement: Cauchy-Davenport theorem. For a prime p and nonempty subsets A and B of Z/pZ, |A + B| ≥ min(p, |A| + |B| - 1).

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on |B| using the Dyson e-transform after translating B so that it meets A but is not contained in A.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on |B|, the case |B| = 1 being immediate.
derive: If A is proper, a nonzero difference d of B moves some element of A outside A, since d generates Z/pZ.
construct: Translate B so that it meets A and has an element outside A.
construct: Replace (A, B) with (A ∪ B, A ∩ B), which keeps the total size and shrinks the sumset.
conclude: The inductive hypothesis gives the bound.

drafts.canonical_statement: For nonempty finite subsets A and B of a linearly ordered abelian group, |A| + |B| ≤ |A + B| + 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compare the two translates A + min B and max A + B, which meet in a single point.
sketch_steps: construct: Let a_0 = max A and b_0 = min B.
derive: A + b_0 and a_0 + B lie in A + B and have sizes |A| and |B|.
derive: Their intersection is the single point a_0 + b_0 by monotonicity.
conclude: Counting the union gives the bound.

sketch_steps: derive: Right translation by an element of B embeds A into A + B.
derive: Left translation by an element of A embeds B into A + B.
conclude: Addition maps A × B onto A + B.

sketch_steps: setup: Fix g and form g - B, which has size |B|.
derive: Since |A| + |B| > |G|, the sets A and g - B intersect.
conclude: An intersection point writes g as a sum.

drafts.proof_strategy: Prove the prime case with Cauchy-Davenport on two-element sets, then induct on the number of prime factors.
sketch_steps: case_split: Dispose of n = 0 and n = 1.
setup: For prime p, sort 2p-1 residues into a_1 ≤ ... ≤ a_{2p-1}.
case_split: Either p consecutive residues coincide, or the pairs {a_i, a_{i+p-1}} have two elements.
apply_theorem: Cauchy-Davenport shows the sum of the pairs covers Z/pZ.
induction: For n = pm, pick 2m-1 disjoint p-subsets with sums divisible by p and apply the case m.

construct: Map (x, b) to (a_x - b, c_x - b).
derive: The difference of the coordinates recovers x, and then b is determined.
conclude: The injection gives the inequality.

drafts.proof_strategy: Pass to a subset of B minimizing the doubling ratio and prove the Plünnecke-Petridis inequality for it by induction.
sketch_steps: case_split: The case of empty B is trivial.
setup: Choose a nonempty subset B' of B minimizing K = |A + B'|/|B'|.
induction: Induction on |D| gives the Plünnecke-Petridis inequality |D + B' + A| ≤ K |D + B'|.
derive: Translation gives |A + C| ≤ |C + B' + A|.
conclude: Since K ≤ |A + B|/|B|, the inequality follows.

sketch_steps: setup: Choose a nonempty A' in A minimizing K' = |A' + B|/|A'|.
induction: Induction on |D| gives the Plünnecke-Petridis inequality |D + A' + B| ≤ K' |D + A'|.
induction: Iterating gives |A' + kB| ≤ K'^k |A'|.
apply_theorem: The Ruzsa triangle inequality bounds |mB - nB| |A'|.
conclude: Dividing and using K' ≤ K and |A'| ≤ |A| gives the bound.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take a maximal subset of A whose translates of B are disjoint.
sketch_steps: construct: Choose a maximal F in A with the translates f + B pairwise disjoint.
derive: Disjoint translates inside A + B give |F| ≤ K.
derive: Maximality makes every a + B meet some f + B.
conclude: Hence a lies in F + (B - B).

drafts.canonical_statement: For finite subsets s, t of an additive abelian group with additive energy E(s,t), the number of quadruples (a,a',b,b') in s × s × t × t with a + b = a' + b', one has |s|^2 |t|^2 ≤ |s + t| E(s,t).

drafts.proof_strategy: Count representations of each sum and apply Cauchy-Schwarz.
sketch_steps: setup: Let r(x) be the number of representations of x as a + b.
derive: The sum of r(x) is |s||t|.
derive: The sum of r(x)^2 is the additive energy.
apply_theorem: Cauchy-Schwarz gives the inequality.

drafts.canonical_statement: Hales-Jewett theorem. For finite sets α and κ there is a finite set ι such that every coloring of the words α^ι by κ has a monochromatic combinatorial line, namely a set of words w_x, x in α, which take the value x on a fixed nonempty set I of coordinates and fixed letters outside I.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the alphabet and, inside that, on the number of color-focused lines.
sketch_steps: case_split: Handle alphabets of size at most 1 directly.
setup: Define r color-focused lines at a point f.
induction: Show that high enough dimension yields a monochromatic line or r focused lines.
construct: Color words on the second block of coordinates by the induced function on the first block.
apply_theorem: Apply the theorem for the smaller alphabet to get a line that makes the coloring independent of the letter.
derive: Lift r focused lines of the induced coloring to r+1 focused lines or a monochromatic line.
conclude: With r equal to the number of colors, the focus has the color of one line, which is then monochromatic.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Hales-Jewett with alphabet S and color each word by the color of its sum.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Hales-Jewett for the alphabet S gives a finite index set.
construct: Color a word by the color of the sum of its letters.
derive: A monochromatic line has sum a s + b with a the number of active coordinates.
conclude: Since the active set is nonempty, a is positive.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Hales-Jewett to the alphabet {0,...,k-1} and color words by the color of their sum.
sketch_steps: setup: Take S = {0,...,k-1} as the alphabet.
apply_theorem: Hales-Jewett gives a monochromatic line for the coloring by the sum of letters.
derive: The sum along a line is b + s a with a the number of active coordinates.
conclude: This is a monochromatic arithmetic progression of length k.

drafts.canonical_statement: Hindman's theorem, assuming the existence of an idempotent ultrafilter on the positive integers. For every finite coloring C of the natural numbers there is a sequence of positive integers (a_i) such that C of the sum over s of a_i is the same color for all nonempty finite sets s of indices.

drafts.proof_strategy: Build the sequence greedily inside a color class that belongs to an idempotent ultrafilter.
sketch_steps: setup: Take an idempotent ultrafilter and a color class A_0 in it.
derive: For A in U, the set A* of x in A with A - x in U again lies in U.
construct: Choose a_n in the star of A_n and define A_{n+1} by intersecting with a shift.
induction: Sums over finite sets with minimum at least n lie in A_n.
conclude: All nonempty finite sums lie in the color class A_0.

sketch_steps: setup: Define the edge energy of a partition, a number between 0 and 1.
apply_theorem: A non-uniform equipartition has an equipartition refinement with energy larger by ε^5/4.
derive: The iteration stops after at most 4 ε^(-5) steps.
derive: The number of parts is bounded in terms of ε and l.
case_split: For few vertices, use the partition into singletons.

drafts.proof_strategy: Clean the graph along a regular partition and use triangle counting on any surviving triangle.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Take a regular equipartition with suitable constants.
construct: Delete edges inside parts, between non-uniform pairs and between sparse pairs.
derive: Fewer than ε n^2 edges are deleted.
derive: A surviving triangle gives three uniform dense pairs, and uniformity then yields many triangles in G.
contradiction: This contradicts the hypothesis for a suitable c(ε).

drafts.canonical_statement: Roth's theorem, assuming the triangle removal lemma. For ε > 0 there is N such that if n ≥ N, A is a subset of {0,...,n-1} and |A| ≥ εn, then A contains a nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression.

drafts.proof_strategy: Encode three-term progressions as triangles of a tripartite graph and apply the removal lemma.
sketch_steps: setup: Assume A has no nontrivial progression and work in Z/MZ with M = 2n+1.
construct: Build a tripartite graph with edges given by differences in A.
derive: Triangles correspond to progressions in A, so only the M|A| trivial ones exist.
derive: Those triangles are edge-disjoint, so removing them needs at least M|A| edges.
apply_theorem: The removal lemma bounds that number, which contradicts |A| ≥ εn for large n.

sketch_steps: derive: Disjointness gives x ≠ y for every pair in s × t.
derive: Each pair is adjacent in exactly one of G and its complement.
conclude: Dividing the edge count identity by |s||t| gives the claim.

sketch_steps: derive: The stronger size condition for ε' implies that for ε.
derive: The density bound below ε gives one below ε'.
derive: Edge density is symmetric in its two arguments.
conclude: Both claims follow from the definition.

drafts.proof_strategy: Sandwich e_1 between e_2 and e_2 + N_1 - N_2 and divide by N_1.

setup: Let x = |s_2||t_2|/(|s_1||t_1|), which is at least (1-δ)^2.
derive: Counting edges gives e_2 ≤ e_1 ≤ e_2 + N_1 - N_2.
derive: Dividing by N_1 gives |d_1 - d_2| ≤ 1 - x.
conclude: This is at most 2δ.

sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The handshake lemma gives the degree sum 2|E|.
derive: All degrees equal k, so the degree sum is k|V|.

drafts.proof_strategy: Sum the degree bounds over all vertices and apply the handshake lemma.
sketch_steps: case_split: The empty vertex set is immediate.
derive: Each degree lies between δ and Δ.
apply_theorem: Summing and using the handshake lemma gives the claim.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finite graph G and a vertex v, deg_G v + deg_{G^c} v + 1 = |V|, where G^c is the complement.

drafts.proof_strategy: Classify the other vertices by adjacency in G or in its complement.
sketch_steps: setup: There are |V| - 1 vertices other than v.
derive: Each is adjacent to v in exactly one of G and its complement.
conclude: Counting gives the identity.

sketch_steps: setup: There are C(n,2) pairs of distinct vertices.
derive: Each pair is an edge of exactly one of G and its complement.
conclude: Summing gives the identity.

sketch_steps: derive: Each edge has exactly one endpoint in s and one in t.
derive: Hence the degree sums over s and over t equal |E|.
derive: Neighbors of a vertex in s lie in t, so its degree is at most |t|.
conclude: Summing gives |E| ≤ |s||t|.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a finite graph, if there is a walk from u to v, then there is a path from u to v of length at most |V| - 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: A shortest walk repeats no vertex, and a path has at most |V| vertices.
sketch_steps: setup: Take a shortest walk from u to v.
contradiction: A repeated vertex would allow a shorter walk.
derive: So the walk is a path with at most |V| vertices.
conclude: Its length is less than |V|.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the length of the walk, removing the initial segment when u reappears.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on the length of the walk.
derive: The rest of the walk contains a path q from x to v.
case_split: Either u is not on q or q passes through u.
conclude: In both cases a path from u to v with the required properties results.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a graph G with nonempty vertex set is not connected, then its complement is connected.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="emptyset"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_connected"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_connected"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_complement"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Vertices in different components are adjacent in the complement; vertices in one component share a neighbor there.
sketch_steps: derive: Vertices not reachable from each other in G are adjacent in the complement.
case_split: Take u and v and split on reachability in G.
construct: If u and v lie in one component, use a vertex outside that component as a middle point.
conclude: The complement is connected.

drafts.canonical_statement: A finite graph G = (V,E) is a tree if and only if it is connected and |E| + 1 = |V|. This contains the edge count formula for trees.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_tree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_connected"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_edges"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the edge count of trees in one direction and prune cycles in the other.
sketch_steps: derive: A tree is connected with |E| + 1 = |V| by removing leaves inductively.
setup: Conversely assume G is connected with |E| + 1 = |V|.
construct: If G has a cycle, deleting cycle edges gives a spanning tree with fewer edges.
contradiction: The spanning tree has |V| - 1 edges, contradicting the edge count.

drafts.canonical_statement: A graph has no cycle if and only if every edge is a bridge, where an edge uv is a bridge when removing it makes v unreachable from u.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_acyclic"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_adjacent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_bridge"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Translate between an edge outside the bridges and a cycle through that edge.
sketch_steps: derive: A non-bridge uv gives a path from v to u avoiding uv of length at least 2.
construct: Adding uv closes this path into a cycle.
derive: An edge of a cycle has an alternative path around the cycle, so it is not a bridge.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: An edge uv of a graph is a bridge if and only if no cycle contains uv.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_adjacent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_bridge"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_edge_on_cycle"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Turn a cycle through uv into a detour, and a detour into a cycle.
sketch_steps: derive: A cycle through uv yields a walk from u to v avoiding uv.
derive: A path from v to u avoiding uv has length at least 2.
construct: Adding uv to that path gives a cycle through uv.
conclude: Contraposition gives the equivalence.

drafts.canonical_statement: A graph without cycles has a proper vertex coloring with two colors.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_acyclic"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_colorable"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Color each vertex by the parity of its unique path length from a root of its component.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose a root in each component; paths to the root are unique.
construct: Color by the parity of the path length.
case_split: For adjacent v and w, either w lies on the path to v or not.
derive: In both cases the path lengths differ by exactly one.
conclude: The coloring is proper.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a set s of vertices of a finite graph G is a clique, then |s| ≤ χ(G). The chromatic number of the complete graph on V is |V|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_clique"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="chromatic_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="chromatic_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="complete_graph_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Vertices of a clique need pairwise distinct colors.
sketch_steps: derive: Colors on a clique are pairwise distinct.
derive: So the number of colors is at least |s|.
construct: Distinct colors on all vertices color the complete graph.
conclude: The complete graph has chromatic number |V|.

drafts.canonical_statement: For n ≥ 2, the cycle graph on Z/nZ joining i to i ± 1 has chromatic number 2 when n is even and 3 when n is odd.

name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="chromatic_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cycle_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>3</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Alternate two colors along the cycle; parity decides whether the last edge is respected.
sketch_steps: derive: An edge exists, so at least two colors are needed.
case_split: Treat n even and n odd.
construct: For even n, color by parity.
contradiction: For odd n, two colors would force the adjacent vertices n-1 and 0 to share a color.
construct: For odd n, a third color on n-1 gives a proper coloring.

drafts.canonical_statement: A graph has chromatic number 2 if and only if it is 2-colorable and has at least one edge.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="chromatic_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_colorable"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_adjacent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: A graph with no edge needs at most one color, and an edge forces two colors.
sketch_steps: derive: Chromatic number 2 gives a 2-coloring.
contradiction: With no edges one color would suffice.
derive: Conversely an edge forces at least two colors.
conclude: Hence the chromatic number is exactly 2.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a finite graph G is k-colorable, then |V| ≤ k α(G), where α(G) is the independence number.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_colorable"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="independence_number"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Color classes are independent sets that partition the vertex set.
sketch_steps: setup: Take a proper coloring with k colors.
derive: Each color class is independent, so its size is at most α(G).
conclude: Summing over the k classes gives the bound.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a triangle-free finite graph, adjacent vertices u and v satisfy deg u + deg v ≤ |V|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_clique_free"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>3</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_adjacent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The neighborhoods of adjacent vertices are disjoint in a triangle-free graph.
sketch_steps: contradiction: A common neighbor of u and v would give a triangle.
derive: So the neighborhoods are disjoint subsets of V.
conclude: Their sizes add up to at most |V|.

drafts.canonical_statement: Mantel's theorem. A triangle-free finite graph with n vertices and m edges satisfies 4m ≤ n^2. This is the case r = 2 of Turán's theorem, proved elementarily.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_clique_free"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>3</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>4</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_edges"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Sum the degree bound over edges and apply Cauchy-Schwarz.
sketch_steps: derive: Adjacent vertices have disjoint neighborhoods, so deg u + deg v ≤ n.
derive: Summing over edges gives the sum of squared degrees at most mn.
apply_theorem: Cauchy-Schwarz and the handshake lemma give a lower bound 4m^2/n.
conclude: Dividing by m gives 4m ≤ n^2.

drafts.canonical_statement: If every edge of a finite graph lies in exactly one triangle, then the number of edges is three times the number of triangles.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="locally_linear_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_edges"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>3</n1:OMI><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_triangles"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Double count pairs consisting of an edge and a triangle containing it.
sketch_steps: setup: Count pairs (e, T) with e an edge of the triangle T.
derive: Each edge occurs in exactly one pair.
derive: Each triangle occurs in exactly three pairs.
conclude: Comparing gives the identity.

drafts.canonical_statement: For the adjacency matrix A of a finite graph over any semiring, the (u,v) entry of A^n equals the number of walks of length n from u to v.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="matrix_entry"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_adjacency_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="walks_of_length"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on n by decomposing a walk into its first step and the rest.
sketch_steps: induction: The case n = 0 is the identity matrix.
derive: Expand the entry of A^(n+1) as a sum over neighbors of u.
derive: A walk of length n+1 splits uniquely into a first step and a walk of length n.
conclude: The entry counts walks of length n+1.

drafts.canonical_statement: For the adjacency matrix A over a commutative semiring of a finite graph, (A^2)_{ii} = deg i, tr A = 0 and tr A^2 = 2|E|.

cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_adjacency_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Expand the diagonal entries and use the handshake lemma.
sketch_steps: derive: The diagonal entry of A^2 counts neighbors of i.
derive: There are no loops, so the trace of A vanishes.
apply_theorem: The handshake lemma gives tr A^2 = 2|E|.

drafts.canonical_statement: For the real Laplacian matrix L = D - A of a finite graph, x^T L x = (1/2) sum over ordered adjacent pairs (i,j) of (x_i - x_j)^2 for x in R^V, and L is positive semidefinite.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dot_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="matrix_vector_mul"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_laplacian_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="edge_difference_square_sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="positive_semidefinite_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_laplacian_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Expand the sum of squared differences and compare it with the degree and adjacency terms.
sketch_steps: derive: Write x^T D x and x^T A x as sums.
derive: Expanding the squares gives twice the degree term minus twice the adjacency term.
conclude: The form is a sum of squares and L is symmetric, so L is positive semidefinite.

drafts.canonical_statement: For the real Laplacian L of a finite graph and x in R^V, Lx = 0 if and only if x_i = x_j whenever j is reachable from i.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="matrix_vector_mul"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_laplacian_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_reachable"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fn_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fn_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the quadratic form for one direction and the entrywise formula for the other.
sketch_steps: derive: Lx = 0 makes the quadratic form vanish, so x agrees on adjacent vertices.
induction: Following a walk, x agrees on reachable vertices.
derive: The i-th entry of Lx is the sum of x_i - x_j over neighbors j of i.
conclude: Constancy on components makes all these sums vanish.

drafts.canonical_statement: The dimension of the kernel of the real Laplacian matrix of a finite graph equals the number of connected components.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="real_kernel_dimension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_laplacian_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="component_count"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The indicator vectors of the connected components form a basis of the kernel.
sketch_steps: setup: Define the indicator vector of each component.
derive: The kernel consists of the vectors constant on each component.
derive: The indicators span the kernel and are linearly independent.
conclude: The dimension equals the number of components.

drafts.canonical_statement: A finite graph with nonempty vertex set is connected if and only if the kernel of its real Laplacian matrix has dimension 1.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="emptyset"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_connected"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="real_kernel_dimension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_laplacian_matrix"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Translate connectivity into a single component and apply the kernel dimension formula.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The kernel dimension equals the number of components.
translate: For a nonempty vertex set, connected means exactly one component.
conclude: Both conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: Perfect matching form of Hall's theorem. If every edge of a finite graph joins two disjoint sets a and b, and |S| ≤ |N(S)| for every vertex set S, then the graph has a perfect matching.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_bipartite_with"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="neighbor_union_size_at_least"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="has_perfect_matching"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show the two sides have equal size and apply Hall's marriage theorem to one side.
sketch_steps: derive: The condition for singletons forces all vertices into a ∪ b.
derive: The condition for a and for b gives |a| = |b|.
apply_theorem: Hall's marriage theorem gives an injection from a to b along edges.
conclude: Equal sizes make it a bijection, which is a perfect matching.

drafts.canonical_statement: For k ≥ 1, every k-regular finite bipartite graph has a perfect matching.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_bipartite_with"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_regular"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="has_perfect_matching"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Double count edges leaving S to verify Hall's condition.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a vertex set S and count adjacent pairs (x, y) with x in S.
derive: Each x in S contributes exactly k pairs.
derive: Each y in N(S) receives at most k pairs.
apply_theorem: The resulting Hall condition gives a perfect matching.

drafts.canonical_statement: Tutte's theorem. A finite graph G has a perfect matching if and only if for every vertex set U the number of connected components of G - U with an odd number of vertices is at most |U|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_simple_graph"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="has_perfect_matching"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="graph_vertices"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="odd_component_count_after_removal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Prove necessity by counting and sufficiency via an edge-maximal counterexample and alternating cycles.
sketch_steps: derive: In a perfect matching, each odd component of G - U has a vertex matched into U.
setup: For sufficiency, take an edge-maximal graph without perfect matching satisfying the condition.
case_split: If G - S is a union of cliques, for S the set of universal vertices, construct a perfect matching directly.
construct: Otherwise pick a, b, c, d and the matchings M_1 of G + ac and M_2 of G + bd.
contradiction: Alternating cycles of M_1 and M_2 yield a perfect matching of G.

drafts.canonical_statement: Uniqueness in Turán's theorem. For r ≥ 1, a finite graph G has the maximum number of edges among graphs on its vertex set without an (r+1)-clique if and only if G is isomorphic to the Turán graph T(n,r), with n = |V|, where T(n,r) joins i, j in {0,...,n-1} when their residues mod r differ.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use symmetrization to show a maximal graph is complete multipartite with balanced parts, then deduce the converse from existence of a maximal graph.
sketch_steps: derive: Nonadjacent vertices have equal degree by the replacement argument.
derive: Nonadjacency is transitive by replacing two adjacent vertices with copies of s.
translate: So the graph is complete multipartite with at most r parts.
derive: Moving or splitting vertices shows the parts are balanced and min(n,r) in number.
conclude: Any maximal graph is isomorphic to T(n,r), which gives both directions.

sketch_steps: case_split: The trivial trail has no edges.
derive: Interior occurrences of x contribute two distinct edges each.
derive: End positions contribute one edge each.
case_split: Compare parity for u ≠ v and u = v.
conclude: This matches the stated condition.

drafts.canonical_statement: A cycle p of a finite graph visits every vertex, that is p is a Hamiltonian cycle, if and only if its length is |V|.

drafts.proof_strategy: A cycle of length m visits exactly m distinct vertices.
sketch_steps: derive: A cycle of length m visits exactly m distinct vertices.
conclude: Those vertices are all of V exactly when m = |V|.

drafts.canonical_statement: A complete graph with at least three vertices has a Hamiltonian cycle.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>3</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="hamiltonian_cycle"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="complete_graph_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: List the vertices in any order and close up the list.
sketch_steps: construct: Arrange the vertices in a sequence.
derive: Consecutive vertices are adjacent in a complete graph.
conclude: With at least three vertices this closes to a cycle through all vertices.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a 2-colorable finite graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, then its number of vertices is even.

drafts.proof_strategy: Colors alternate along the closed walk, so its length is even.
sketch_steps: derive: The length of a Hamiltonian cycle is |V|.
derive: Colors alternate along each step of the cycle.
conclude: Returning to the start forces an even number of steps.

drafts.canonical_statement: The Cayley graph of a group M with respect to a subset s, joining x ≠ y when x^(-1) y or y^(-1) x lies in s, is connected if and only if s generates M.

drafts.proof_strategy: Walks correspond to products of generators and their inverses.
sketch_steps: derive: Along a walk, a^(-1) b is a product of elements of s and their inverses.
conclude: Connectivity from 1 shows every element lies in the generated subgroup.
induction: Conversely, by induction on the subgroup, y reaches y x for every x in H.
conclude: Taking x = u^(-1) v connects any two vertices.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use monotonicity of the radical for one inclusion and multiply powers for the other.
sketch_steps: derive: Since IJ lies in the intersection and the intersection lies in I and J, the radicals are nested.
setup: Take x with x^m in I and x^n in J.
derive: Then x^(m+n) is a product of an element of I and an element of J, so it lies in IJ.
conclude: All three radicals coincide.

drafts.canonical_statement: If ideals I and J of a commutative ring R satisfy rad(I) + rad(J) = R, then I + J = R.
