drafts.proof_strategy: A proper sum would lie in a maximal ideal, which then contains both radicals.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose I + J is proper and choose a maximal ideal M containing it.
derive: M is prime, so it contains the radicals of I and of J.
contradiction: The sum of the radicals is R and lies in M.
conclude: Hence I + J = R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take the contrapositive and multiply one witness from each ideal.
sketch_steps: derive: If one member lies in P, the intersection does too.
setup: Otherwise pick x_i in I_i outside P for each i.
derive: The product lies in every I_i, and it equals 1 for the empty family.
derive: Primality keeps the product outside P.
conclude: The intersection is not contained in P.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the number of ideals and combine witnesses that avoid all but one ideal.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on the number n of ideals; deleting one ideal keeps the hypothesis.
setup: If I lies in no J_i, the induction gives x_i in I avoiding every J_j with j different from i, and then x_i lies in J_i.
case_split: For n = 2 the sum x_1 + x_2 avoids both ideals.
case_split: For n at least 3 choose J_1 prime and form y = x_1 + x_2 ... x_n.
derive: Primality of J_1 gives y outside J_1, and y is outside each other J_j.
contradiction: The element y of I lies outside the union.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring R, the quotient R/I is reduced if and only if the radical of I equals I.

drafts.proof_strategy: Translate nilpotence in the quotient into a power lying in the ideal.
sketch_steps: translate: The class of x has vanishing n-th power exactly when x^n lies in I.
derive: If R/I is reduced, every element of the radical lies in I.
derive: If I is its own radical, every nilpotent class is zero.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: For ideals I, J and K of a commutative ring, with (I:J) the ideal of all r such that rJ lies in I, one has ((I:J):K) = (I:JK).

drafts.proof_strategy: Compare both sides on products of generators, using that IJ is spanned by products.
sketch_steps: setup: Take x in ((I:J):K), y in J and z in K.
derive: Then xzy lies in I, and finite sums of products yz fill JK.
derive: Conversely x in (I:JK) gives (xz)y in I for all y in J.
conclude: The two ideals are equal.

drafts.proof_strategy: Rewrite membership in (Q:x) as a product lying in Q and apply the primary condition.
sketch_steps: translate: a lies in J = (Q:x) exactly when ax lies in Q.
derive: If a^n x lies in Q and x is outside Q, then a^n lies in rad(Q), so rad(J) = rad(Q).
derive: J is proper since 1 in J would put x in Q.
derive: If ab lies in J, then (ax)b lies in Q, so ax lies in Q or b lies in rad(Q).
conclude: J is primary with radical rad(Q).

drafts.canonical_statement: If an ideal I of a commutative ring is disjoint from a multiplicative submonoid M, then some prime ideal contains I and is disjoint from M.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Zorn to ideals disjoint from M and show a maximal one is prime.
sketch_steps: setup: Let Sigma be the set of ideals containing I and disjoint from M.
apply_theorem: Unions of chains stay in Sigma, so Zorn gives a maximal element P.
derive: P is proper because 1 lies in M.
derive: If a and b are outside P, then P + (a) and P + (b) meet M.
derive: Multiplying the two elements of M gives an element of M in P + (ab).
conclude: So ab is outside P and P is prime.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every element x of a minimal prime ideal of a commutative ring is a zero divisor, that is, xy = 0 for some nonzero y.

drafts.proof_strategy: Show 0 lies in the multiplicative set generated by x and the complement of P, then take a minimal power.
sketch_steps: setup: Let T be the set of all s x^n with s outside P.
contradiction: If 0 is not in T, a prime disjoint from T lies strictly inside P.
derive: Hence s x^n = 0 for some s outside P and some n.
construct: For the least such n, put y = s x^(n-1).
conclude: Then y is nonzero and xy = 0.

construct: For j different from i write 1 = a_j + b_j with a_j in I_j and b_j in I_i.
derive: The product e_i of the a_j is 1 mod I_i and lies in every other I_j.
derive: The combination of the c_i e_i has residues c_i.
conclude: The homomorphism theorem gives the isomorphism.

drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the family, using that an ideal coprime to each factor is coprime to the product.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on the size of s; the empty case is the whole ring on both sides.
derive: Expanding the product of 1 = u_i + v_i shows J_a + B = R for B the product over the rest.
derive: For coprime A and B, the identity 1 = a + b gives that the intersection equals AB.
conclude: The induction hypothesis finishes the step.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nonzero commutative ring R is local if and only if for every x in R, either x or 1 - x is a unit.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use that nonunits lie in maximal ideals and that distinct maximal ideals are comaximal.
sketch_steps: derive: In a local ring, x and 1 - x both nonunits would put 1 in the maximal ideal.
setup: For the converse, suppose two distinct maximal ideals exist.
derive: Comaximality gives 1 = a + b with a and b in the two ideals.
contradiction: Then a and 1 - a are both nonunits.
conclude: The maximal ideal is unique.

drafts.canonical_statement: If M is a maximal ideal of a commutative ring R and 1 + a is a unit for every a in M, then R is local and M is exactly the set of nonunits.

drafts.proof_strategy: Show every element outside M is a unit by comaximality with M.
sketch_steps: derive: Elements of the proper ideal M are nonunits.
setup: For x outside M, maximality gives xy + a = 1 with a in M.
derive: Then xy = 1 + (-a) is a unit, so x is a unit.
derive: Every maximal ideal consists of nonunits and hence lies in M.
conclude: M is the unique maximal ideal and equals the set of nonunits.

drafts.canonical_statement: An idempotent e of a commutative local ring is 0 or 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: One of e and 1 - e is a unit, and their product vanishes.
sketch_steps: derive: The product e(1 - e) is zero.
derive: In a local ring e and 1 - e cannot both be nonunits.
case_split: Cancel the unit factor in each case.
conclude: So e = 1 or e = 0.

sketch_steps: construct: Set h of a/s to be g(a) g(s)^(-1).
derive: If a/s = b/t then uta = usb for some u in M, and g(u) is a unit, so the values agree.
derive: Sums and products are checked over common denominators.
derive: Any h with h ∘ φ = g sends φ(s)^(-1) to g(s)^(-1).
conclude: So h exists and is unique.

derive: Conversely, the kernel description gives y = 0 from φ(y) = 0.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compute the contraction by clearing denominators with M, then transfer primality.
sketch_steps: setup: Elements of PS have the form φ(a) φ(s)^(-1) with a in P.
derive: If φ(x) lies in PS, then usx lies in P for some u in M, so x lies in P.
derive: Hence the contraction equals P, and PS is proper.
derive: A product of two fractions in PS has numerator product in P.
conclude: Primality of P gives primality of PS.

drafts.proof_strategy: Extend Q to S when it avoids the complement of P, and use units for the converse.
sketch_steps: setup: Put M = R \ P, so φ(M) consists of units.
construct: For Q inside P let J be the extension of Q to S.
derive: Clearing denominators shows the contraction of J is Q and that J is prime.
derive: Conversely an element of the contraction outside P would make J contain a unit.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.proof_strategy: Study the ideal of multipliers taking x into J and show no maximal ideal contains it.
sketch_steps: derive: The forward direction follows by extending generators.
setup: For x in I let D be the ideal of r with rx in J.
contradiction: If D lies in a maximal ideal P, the inclusion in R_P gives usx = ub with u and s outside P.
derive: Then us lies in D but outside P.
conclude: So 1 lies in D and x lies in J.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let R be an integral domain with fraction field K and canonical map φ. If x in K can be written with φ(s) x = φ(a), a in R and s outside P, for every maximal ideal P of R, then x lies in φ(R).

drafts.proof_strategy: Consider the ideal of denominators of x and show it is not contained in any maximal ideal.
sketch_steps: setup: Let D be the ideal of all s with φ(s) x in φ(R).
contradiction: If D were proper it would lie in a maximal ideal P, against the denominator s outside P.
derive: Therefore 1 lies in D.
conclude: So x lies in φ(R).

drafts.canonical_statement: For ideals I and J of a commutative ring, the closed subsets V(I) and V(J) of the prime spectrum coincide if and only if the radicals of I and J coincide.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use that a prime contains an ideal exactly when it contains its radical, and that the radical is the intersection of the primes containing the ideal.
sketch_steps: derive: A prime contains I if and only if it contains rad(I), so V(I) = V(rad(I)).
apply_theorem: The radical of I is the intersection of all primes in V(I).
conclude: Hence V(I) and rad(I) determine each other.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an element f of a commutative ring, the basic open set D(f) of primes not containing f is empty if and only if f is nilpotent.

drafts.proof_strategy: Empty D(f) means f lies in every prime; separate a non-nilpotent f from a prime using its powers.
sketch_steps: translate: D(f) is empty exactly when f lies in every prime ideal.
derive: A nilpotent element lies in every prime.
setup: If f is not nilpotent, its powers form a submonoid not containing 0.
apply_theorem: Some prime is disjoint from that submonoid.
conclude: That prime lies in D(f).

drafts.canonical_statement: For elements f and g of a commutative ring, D(f) ⊆ D(g) holds in the prime spectrum if and only if f lies in the radical of the principal ideal (g).

drafts.proof_strategy: Rewrite the inclusion of complements and apply the description of the radical by primes.
sketch_steps: translate: D(f) ⊆ D(g) says every prime containing g contains f.
apply_theorem: The radical of (g) is the intersection of the primes containing g.
conclude: This is the statement that f lies in that radical.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring, the closed subset V(I) of the prime spectrum is irreducible if and only if the radical of I is a prime ideal.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="spectrum_zero_locus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The radical is the generic point when prime, and primality follows from covering V(I) by V(x) and V(y).
sketch_steps: setup: Irreducible means nonempty and not covered by two closed sets without lying in one of them.
derive: If rad(I) is prime it is a point of V(I), and any closed set containing it contains V(I).
derive: If V(I) is irreducible, then rad(I) is proper.
derive: From xy in rad(I), V(I) lies in V(x) ∪ V(y), hence in one of them.
conclude: So rad(I) is prime.

drafts.canonical_statement: For points x and y of Spec R with corresponding prime ideals P_x and P_y, the point y lies in the closure of {x} if and only if P_x ⊆ P_y.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_spectrum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_spectrum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="set_closure"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="singleton_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="spectrum_point_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="spectrum_point_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Identify the closure of a point with the zero locus of its prime ideal.
sketch_steps: translate: A closed set V(E) contains x exactly when E lies in P_x.
derive: Every such V(E) contains V(P_x), and V(P_x) is itself closed and contains x.
derive: So the closure of {x} is V(P_x).
conclude: Membership of y means P_x lies in P_y.

drafts.canonical_statement: An element x of a commutative R-algebra A is integral over R if and only if the subalgebra R[x] is a finitely generated R-module.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_adjoin_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce high powers with the monic relation, and use the determinant trick for the converse.
sketch_steps: derive: A monic relation of degree n expresses all powers of x through 1, x, ..., x^(n-1).
setup: If y_1, ..., y_k generate R[x], write x y_i as a combination of the y_j.
construct: Form the matrix B = xE - (a_ij), which kills the vector (y_j).
derive: Multiplying by the adjugate gives det(B) y_j = 0 for all j.
derive: Since 1 lies in R[x], det(B) = 0.
conclude: det(B) is a monic polynomial in x with coefficients from R.

drafts.canonical_statement: A commutative algebra S of finite type over a commutative ring R is a finitely generated R-module if and only if S is integral over R.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_type_algebra"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the determinant trick on module generators, and bound exponents with the monic relations.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose y_1, ..., y_k generate S as an R-module and take x in S.
derive: The matrix xE - (a_ij) kills (y_j), so its determinant kills S and vanishes.
derive: That determinant is a monic relation for x.
setup: Conversely write S = R[x_1, ..., x_n] with monic relations of degrees d_i.
conclude: Monomials with exponents below d_i generate S as an R-module.

drafts.canonical_statement: If φ from R to S is an injective ring homomorphism of commutative rings making S integral over R, and φ(r) is a unit of S, then r is a unit of R.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ring_hom_injective"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fn_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Multiply the integral equation of the inverse by a power of φ(r) to place the inverse in φ(R).
sketch_steps: setup: Let y be the inverse of φ(r) and take a monic relation of degree n for y.
case_split: For n = 0 both rings are zero and the claim is trivial.
derive: Multiplying by φ(r)^(n-1) expresses y as φ(t) with t in R.
derive: Then φ(rt) = 1.
conclude: Injectivity gives rt = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a ring homomorphism φ from R to S makes S integral over R, then a prime ideal Q of S is maximal if and only if its contraction φ^(-1)(Q) is maximal.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="integral_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_comap"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebra_map"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Pass to the integral extension of domains R/P inside S/Q and compare the field property on both sides.
sketch_steps: translate: Maximality of Q and of P means S/Q and R/P are fields.
derive: R/P embeds in S/Q and the extension of domains is integral.
derive: If the base is a field, a minimal monic relation has nonzero constant term, so nonzero elements invert.
derive: If the top is a field, the inverse of a nonzero a in the base lies in the base by multiplying with a^(n-1).
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.canonical_statement: A commutative ring is Noetherian if and only if every nonempty set of its ideals has a maximal element with respect to inclusion.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="subset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="all_ideals"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="emptyset"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="not"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="prsubset"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Convert a set without maximal element into a strictly ascending chain, and maximize among finitely generated subideals.
sketch_steps: setup: If a nonempty set has no maximal element, choose a strictly ascending chain in it.
contradiction: Finite generators of the union lie in one term of the chain.
setup: Conversely take a maximal finitely generated subideal J of I.
contradiction: An element of I outside J would enlarge J.
conclude: Hence I is finitely generated.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every surjective ring endomorphism of a commutative Noetherian ring is injective.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ring_hom"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="surjective"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ring_hom_injective"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Stabilize the chain of kernels of the powers of f and pull an element of ker f back through f^n.
sketch_steps: setup: The kernels of the powers of f form an ascending chain of ideals.
derive: Noetherianity gives n with ker f^n = ker f^(n+1).
derive: For x in ker f write x = f^n(y) by surjectivity.
derive: Then y lies in ker f^(n+1) = ker f^n.
conclude: So x = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every ideal I of a commutative Noetherian ring contains some power of its radical.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take a finite generating set of the radical and apply the pigeonhole principle to exponents.
sketch_steps: setup: The radical is finitely generated by x_1, ..., x_k with x_i^(d_i) in I.
construct: Put n = d_1 + ... + d_k.
derive: Every monomial of total degree n has some exponent e_i at least d_i.
conclude: So all generators of the n-th power of the radical lie in I.

drafts.canonical_statement: Cohen's theorem. If every prime ideal of a commutative ring is finitely generated, then the ring is Noetherian.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: A maximal non-finitely-generated ideal is prime, by writing it through P + (a) and the colon ideal (P:a).
sketch_steps: setup: If R is not Noetherian, Zorn gives an ideal P maximal among those not finitely generated.
contradiction: Suppose a and b lie outside P with ab in P.
derive: P + (a) has generators p_i + r_i a with p_i in P.
derive: The colon D = (P:a) strictly contains P, so it is finitely generated.
derive: Every x in P lies in (p_1, ..., p_n) + aD, so P is finitely generated.
conclude: Thus P is prime and not finitely generated, against the hypothesis.

drafts.canonical_statement: Krull's principal ideal theorem. If R is a commutative Noetherian ring, x an element of R and P a prime ideal minimal over (x), then the height of P is at most 1.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_prime_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="principal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_height"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce to a local domain, stabilize symbolic powers modulo x using Artinianity, and apply Nakayama twice.
sketch_steps: setup: From a chain P ⊋ Q ⊋ Q' pass to the local domain R_P/Q'R_P, where P is the only prime containing x.
derive: R/(x) is Noetherian with a single prime, so it is Artinian.
derive: The chain Q^(n) + (x) of symbolic powers stabilizes at some n.
derive: Since x is outside Q, this yields Q^(n) = Q^(n+1) + x Q^(n).
apply_theorem: Nakayama over R gives Q^(n) = Q^(n+1).
apply_theorem: Extending to R_Q and using Nakayama again gives Q^n R_Q = 0.
contradiction: In a domain this forces Q = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a commutative Artinian ring, an element x such that xy = 0 implies y = 0 is a unit.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="artinian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Stabilize the descending chain of powers of x and cancel x.
sketch_steps: derive: The chain of principal ideals (x^n) stabilizes, so x^n = x^(n+1) y.
derive: Then x^n (1 - xy) = 0.
derive: Cancelling x repeatedly gives 1 - xy = 0.
conclude: So x is a unit.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every element of a commutative Artinian local ring is a unit or nilpotent.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="artinian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="local_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="or"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nilpotent_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Stabilize powers of x and note that 1 - xy is a unit in a local ring.
sketch_steps: setup: Take a nonunit x, which lies in the maximal ideal M.
derive: The chain (x^n) stabilizes, so x^n (1 - xy) = 0.
derive: Since xy lies in M, 1 - xy is a unit.
conclude: So x^n = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the descending chain condition to get finitely many maximal ideals and a nilpotent Jacobson radical, then apply the Chinese remainder theorem.
sketch_steps: derive: A minimal finite intersection of maximal ideals forces finitely many maximal ideals.
setup: Let J be their intersection and A a stable power of J, so A^2 = A.
contradiction: If A is nonzero, a minimal ideal B with AB nonzero is principal and gives x = ax with a in J.
derive: Since 1 - a is a unit, x = 0, so J is nilpotent.
derive: Reducedness gives J = 0.
apply_theorem: The Chinese remainder theorem gives the isomorphism.

drafts.canonical_statement: If U is a finitely generated submodule of an R-module and U ⊆ IU for an ideal I of the commutative ring R, then there is r in R with r - 1 in I and rU = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the determinant trick to the matrix E - (a_ij) with entries a_ij in I.
sketch_steps: setup: Write u_i as a combination of the generators u_j with coefficients in I.
construct: The matrix B = E - (a_ij) kills the vector (u_j).
derive: Multiplying by the adjugate gives det(B) u_j = 0 for all j.
derive: Modulo I the determinant equals 1.
conclude: Take r = det(B).

drafts.canonical_statement: A finitely generated ideal I of a commutative ring satisfies I^2 = I if and only if I = (e) for some element e with e^2 = e.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finitely_generated_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_product"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="principal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the determinant trick on I = I · I to obtain an element acting as the identity on I.
sketch_steps: derive: If I = (e) with e idempotent, then I^2 = I.
setup: Conversely write the generators of I as combinations with coefficients in I.
derive: The determinant trick gives r congruent to 1 mod I with rI = 0.
construct: Put e = 1 - r, which lies in I and acts as the identity on I.
conclude: Thus I = (e) and e^2 = e.

drafts.canonical_statement: For ideals I and J of a commutative ring, the radical of I + J equals the radical of rad(I) + rad(J).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_sum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use monotonicity of the radical in both directions together with idempotence of the radical.
sketch_steps: derive: I + J lies in rad(I) + rad(J), so its radical lies in the radical of rad(I) + rad(J).
derive: rad(I) and rad(J) lie in rad(I + J), hence so does their sum.
derive: The radical is idempotent, since a power of a power is a power.
conclude: Both inclusions give the equality.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring R, rad(I) = R if and only if I = R.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="unit_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Test the unit element: a power of 1 is 1.
sketch_steps: derive: If I = R then rad(I) contains I and is R.
setup: If rad(I) = R then 1 lies in rad(I).
conclude: So 1 = 1^n lies in I and I = R.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring and an integer n ≥ 1, the radical of I^n equals the radical of I.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="N"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_radical"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use I^n ⊆ I for one inclusion and raise a power in I to the n-th power for the other.
sketch_steps: derive: Since n ≥ 1, I^n lies in I, so rad(I^n) lies in rad(I).
setup: Take x with x^m in I.
derive: Then x^(mn) = (x^m)^n lies in I^n.
conclude: Hence rad(I) lies in rad(I^n).

drafts.proof_strategy: Take a common exponent, which exists because the family is finite.
sketch_steps: derive: The intersection lies in each F_i, so the left side lies in the right side.
setup: Take x with x^(m_i) in F_i for each i.
derive: With m the maximum of the m_i, x^m lies in every F_i.
conclude: So x lies in the radical of the intersection.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a unital homomorphism f from R to S of commutative rings and an ideal K of S, the preimage of rad(K) is the radical of the preimage of K.

drafts.proof_strategy: Unfold both memberships and use that f preserves powers.
sketch_steps: setup: Take x in R.
translate: x lies in the preimage of rad(K) iff f(x)^n lies in K for some n.
derive: f(x)^n = f(x^n), so this says x^n lies in the preimage of K.
conclude: The two ideals have the same elements.

drafts.proof_strategy: Choose elements outside P in each factor and multiply them.
sketch_steps: derive: If F_i lies in P, the product, which lies in F_i, lies in P.
setup: Otherwise pick x_i in F_i outside P for each i.
derive: Their product is outside P because P is prime and proper.
conclude: That product lies in the product ideal, so the product ideal is not in P.

drafts.canonical_statement: If I is a finitely generated ideal of a commutative ring and I lies in the radical of an ideal J, then I^n lies in J for some n. This generalizes the corresponding Noetherian statement about a power of the radical.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take exponents for the generators and apply the pigeonhole principle to monomials of degree n.
sketch_steps: setup: Write I = (a_1, ..., a_r) and choose m_k with a_k^(m_k) in J.
construct: Let n be the sum of the m_k.
derive: I^n is spanned by monomials of total degree n in the a_k.
derive: By pigeonhole each monomial has e_k ≥ m_k for some k, so it lies in J.
conclude: Hence I^n lies in J.

drafts.proof_strategy: Prove the two inclusions directly and derive the two equalities from them by monotonicity.
sketch_steps: derive: x in I has f(x) in I^e, so I lies in I^ec.
derive: K^ce is generated by a subset of K, so it lies in K.
derive: Extending the first inclusion and specializing the second gives I^ece = I^e.
derive: Specializing the first and contracting the second gives K^cec = K^c.
conclude: All four claims hold.

drafts.canonical_statement: A nonzero commutative ring R has exactly one maximal ideal if and only if a sum of two nonunits of R is always a nonunit.

drafts.proof_strategy: Show that the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal in each direction.
sketch_steps: derive: A nonunit generates a proper ideal, which lies in a maximal ideal.
conclude: If m is the only maximal ideal, the nonunits are exactly m, so they are closed under addition.
setup: Conversely let n be the set of nonunits.
derive: n contains 0, is closed under addition by hypothesis and under multiplication by R.
derive: Every proper ideal consists of nonunits, so it lies in n.
conclude: Hence n is the unique maximal ideal.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let I be an ideal of a commutative ring and P a prime ideal containing I. Then P contains a prime ideal minimal among the primes containing I.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply Zorn's lemma to the primes between I and P ordered by reverse inclusion.
sketch_steps: setup: Let Σ be the set of primes Q with I ⊆ Q ⊆ P, ordered by reverse inclusion.
derive: The intersection of a chain of primes in Σ is prime and contains I.
apply_theorem: Zorn's lemma gives a minimal element Q of Σ.
derive: A prime between I and Q lies in Σ, so it equals Q.
conclude: Q is minimal over I and lies in P.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring R, rad(I) is the intersection of the primes minimal over I, the empty intersection being R when I = R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compare with the description of the radical as the intersection of all primes containing I.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: rad(I) is the intersection of all primes containing I.
derive: Minimal primes over I are among them, which gives one inclusion.
apply_theorem: Each prime containing I contains a minimal prime over I.
conclude: So intersecting over minimal primes gives the same ideal.

sketch_steps: derive: A prime contains I + J iff it contains both I and J.
derive: IJ ⊆ I ∩ J ⊆ I, J gives V(I) ∪ V(J) ⊆ V(I ∩ J) ⊆ V(IJ).
derive: A prime containing IJ contains I or J.
conclude: The three sets agree.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring R, the closed set V(I) of the prime spectrum is empty if and only if I = R.

drafts.proof_strategy: A proper ideal lies in a maximal ideal, which is prime.
sketch_steps: derive: If I = R, no prime contains 1, so V(I) is empty.
apply_theorem: If I is proper, it lies in a maximal ideal.
conclude: That maximal ideal is a point of V(I).

drafts.canonical_statement: For an ideal I of a commutative ring R, the intersection of all points of V(I), that is the vanishing ideal of V(I), equals rad(I).

drafts.proof_strategy: This is the description of the radical as the intersection of the primes containing the ideal.
sketch_steps: derive: If x^n lies in I, then x lies in every prime containing I.
setup: If x is outside rad(I), the powers of x form a multiplicative set disjoint from I.
apply_theorem: An ideal maximal among those containing I and disjoint from it is prime.
conclude: This prime contains I but not x.

drafts.canonical_statement: The basic open sets D(f), for f in a commutative ring R, form a basis of the Zariski topology on Spec R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Write an open set as the complement of V(s) and pick an element of s outside the given prime.
sketch_steps: derive: D(f) is the complement of V({f}), so it is open.
setup: Let U be open with complement V(s), and p a point of U.
construct: Since p is not in V(s), choose f in s outside p.
conclude: Then p lies in D(f), and D(f) lies in U.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an element f of a commutative ring R, the basic open set D(f) is quasi-compact. This generalizes quasi-compactness of Spec R = D(1).

drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce to covers by basic opens and translate covering into f lying in the radical of the generated ideal.
sketch_steps: setup: Since basic opens form a basis, take a cover of D(f) by D(g_i).
derive: Every prime containing all g_i contains f, so f lies in the radical of (g_i).
construct: Write f^n as a finite combination of the g_i.
conclude: The finitely many g_i appearing already cover D(f).

derive: fg lies in p iff f or g lies in p, which gives D(fg) = D(f) ∩ D(g).
derive: For n ≥ 1, f^n lies in p iff f lies in p.
conclude: Hence D(f^n) = D(f).

apply_theorem: V(J) is empty iff J = R, since a proper ideal lies in a maximal ideal.
conclude: The two conditions are equivalent.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take the intersection of the points of Z as the generic point and use closures of points.
sketch_steps: setup: Let p be the intersection of all points of Z.
derive: Irreducibility of Z makes p a prime ideal.
derive: Since Z = V(J) is closed, J lies in p, so p is a point of Z.
derive: The closure of p is V(p), and it equals Z.
conclude: Two primes with the same closure contain each other, so the point is unique.

drafts.canonical_statement: The irreducible components of the prime spectrum of a commutative ring R are exactly the sets V(p) with p a minimal prime ideal of R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Irreducible closed subsets correspond to primes with reversed order, so maximal ones correspond to minimal primes.
sketch_steps: derive: Irreducible components are closed because the closure of an irreducible set is irreducible.
derive: V(p) is the closure of a point, hence irreducible.
derive: Every irreducible closed set has the form V(p) with p prime.
derive: V(p) ⊆ V(q) iff q ⊆ p, so the correspondence reverses order.
conclude: Maximal irreducible closed sets correspond to minimal primes.

drafts.canonical_statement: If R is a Noetherian commutative ring, then Spec R is a Noetherian topological space, that is, every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="prime_spectrum"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Pass to the ascending chain of vanishing ideals and use V(I(Z)) = Z for closed Z.
sketch_steps: setup: Take a descending chain of closed sets Z_i.
derive: The ideals I(Z_i) form an ascending chain.
apply_theorem: This chain stabilizes because R is Noetherian.
derive: For closed Z one has V(I(Z)) = Z.
conclude: So the chain of closed sets stabilizes.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a unital homomorphism f from R to S of commutative rings, with induced map f* from Spec S to Spec R, the preimage of V(s) is V(f(s)) and the preimage of D(x) is D(f(x)); in particular f* is continuous.

drafts.proof_strategy: Unfold membership of the contraction of a prime ideal.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a prime q of S.
translate: The contraction of q contains s iff q contains f(s).
translate: The contraction of q omits x iff q omits f(x).
conclude: The preimage formulas hold, and closed sets pull back to closed sets.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f from R to S is a surjective unital homomorphism of commutative rings, then f* from Spec S to Spec R is a closed embedding with image V(ker f).

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the correspondence between ideals of S and ideals of R containing the kernel.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Primes of S correspond to primes of R containing ker f.
derive: So f* is injective with image V(ker f).
derive: The image of V(J) is V(f^(-1)(J)), so f* is a closed map.
conclude: An injective continuous closed map is a closed embedding.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an element r of a commutative ring R and S the localization of R at the powers of r, the map Spec S to Spec R is an open embedding with image D(r).

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the prime correspondence for localization and compute the image of basic opens.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Primes of S correspond to primes of R not meeting the powers of r.
derive: These are the primes not containing r, so the image is D(r).
derive: Every element of S is a unit multiple of the image of some a in R.
derive: The image of D(φ(a)) is D(ar), which is open.
conclude: An injective continuous open map is an open embedding.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a unital homomorphism f from R to S of commutative rings, the image of f* is dense in Spec R if and only if ker f lies in the nilradical of R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compute the closure of the image as V of the preimage of the nilradical of S.
sketch_steps: setup: Let A be the intersection of the primes in the image of f*.
derive: The closure of the image is V(A).
derive: A is the preimage of the nilradical of S.
derive: Density means A lies in the nilradical of R.
conclude: This is equivalent to ker f lying in the nilradical, since f(x) nilpotent means some x^n lies in ker f.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f from R to S is a unital homomorphism of commutative rings making S integral over f(R), then f* from Spec S to Spec R is a closed map.

drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce to the injective integral map modulo J and apply lying over.
sketch_steps: setup: Take a closed set V(J) of Spec S.
derive: Its image lies in V(f^(-1)(J)).
derive: The induced map from R/f^(-1)(J) to S/J is injective and integral.
apply_theorem: Lying over gives a prime of S/J above any given prime.
conclude: So the image equals V(f^(-1)(J)), which is closed.

drafts.proof_strategy: Write s and its complement as finite unions of basic opens, then split 1 using coprime powers.
sketch_steps: derive: For idempotent e, Spec R is the disjoint union of D(e) and D(1-e).
setup: For clopen s, quasi-compactness gives finite covers of s and its complement, with ideals I and J.
derive: I + J = R and IJ is nilpotent.
construct: Choose n with (IJ)^n = 0 and write 1 = e + g with e in I^n and g in J^n.
derive: Then eg = 0, so e is idempotent.
conclude: D(e) lies in s and D(g) lies in its complement, so D(e) = s.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a nonzero commutative ring R, Spec R is connected if and only if the only idempotents of R are 0 and 1.

drafts.proof_strategy: Combine the correspondence between clopen subsets and idempotents with the extreme cases D(e) = ∅ and D(e) = Spec R.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Clopen subsets of Spec R are exactly the D(e) for idempotent e.
derive: If D(e) is empty, e is nilpotent, and an idempotent nilpotent is 0.
derive: If D(e) is everything, e is a unit, and an idempotent unit is 1.
conclude: So connectedness is equivalent to having only the trivial idempotents.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a commutative ring R with nilradical n, the map Spec(R/n) to Spec R induced by the quotient map is a homeomorphism.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the closed embedding of a surjection and note that the nilradical lies in every prime.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: For the surjection π, the map π* is a closed embedding with image V(ker π).
derive: The kernel is the nilradical, which lies in every prime.
derive: So V(ker π) is all of Spec R.
conclude: A surjective closed embedding is a homeomorphism.

drafts.canonical_statement: If M is a module over a commutative ring R and the localization of M at every maximal ideal of R vanishes, then M = 0.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="zero_module_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="localized_module"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="zero_module_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The annihilator of a nonzero element lies in a maximal ideal, where the element cannot vanish after localizing.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose x in M is nonzero.
derive: Its annihilator is a proper ideal, so it lies in a maximal ideal m.
derive: x/1 = 0 in M_m gives s outside m with sx = 0.
contradiction: Then s lies in the annihilator, which lies in m.
conclude: So M = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let x be an element of a module M over a commutative ring R. If the image x/1 of x in M_m is zero for every maximal ideal m, then x = 0.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="module_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="localized_element"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show the annihilator of x is contained in no maximal ideal.
sketch_steps: setup: Let A be the annihilator of x.
derive: For each maximal m, x/1 = 0 gives s outside m with sx = 0.
derive: So A is contained in no maximal ideal.
conclude: Hence A = R and x = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f from M to N is a linear map of modules over a commutative ring R and the localization of f at every maximal ideal is injective, then f is injective.

drafts.proof_strategy: Localize an element of the kernel at each maximal ideal and apply the local-global principle for elements.
sketch_steps: setup: Take x with f(x) = 0.
derive: Injectivity of f_m gives x/1 = 0 in M_m for each maximal m.
derive: So the annihilator of x lies in no maximal ideal.
conclude: Hence x = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f from M to N is a linear map of modules over a commutative ring R and the localization of f at every maximal ideal is surjective, then f is surjective.

drafts.proof_strategy: Consider the ideal of denominators r with ry in the image and show it lies in no maximal ideal.
sketch_steps: setup: For y in N, let A be the ideal of r with ry in f(M).
derive: Surjectivity of f_m gives y/1 = f(x)/s, so tsy = f(tx) for some t outside m.
derive: Thus ts lies in A but not in m.
conclude: A = R, so y lies in f(M).

drafts.canonical_statement: If the localization of a commutative ring R at every maximal ideal is reduced, then R is reduced.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="maximal_ideal"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="localization_at_prime"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="reduced_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="reduced_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Send a nilpotent to each local ring, where it vanishes, then use the annihilator argument.
sketch_steps: setup: Let x be nilpotent in R.
derive: x/1 is nilpotent in the reduced ring R_m, so x/1 = 0.
derive: The annihilator of x lies in no maximal ideal.
conclude: So x = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: If R is an integral domain and the localization of R at every maximal ideal is integrally closed, then R is integrally closed.

drafts.proof_strategy: An integral element lies in every localization, and the ideal of denominators is then the unit ideal.
sketch_steps: setup: Let x in the fraction field be integral over R.
derive: x is integral over each R_m, so x lies in each R_m.
setup: Let A be the ideal of r with rx in R.
derive: Writing x = a/s with s outside m shows s lies in A, so A is not in m.
conclude: A = R, so x lies in R.

drafts.proof_strategy: Test flatness on an injection, localize at each maximal ideal, and use the local criterion for injectivity.
sketch_steps: setup: Take an injection g from N' to N.
derive: g_m is injective because localization is exact.
derive: (id ⊗ g)_m identifies with id ⊗ g_m over R_m, which is injective by flatness of M_m.
apply_theorem: Injectivity of a linear map is checked at maximal ideals.
conclude: So id ⊗ g is injective and M is flat.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let R be an integrally closed domain, M a multiplicative subset not containing 0, and S the localization of R at M. Then S is integrally closed.

drafts.proof_strategy: Clear denominators in an integral equation to get an equation over R for a multiple of x.
sketch_steps: setup: Let x in K satisfy a monic equation with coefficients a_i/s_i in S.
construct: Let s be the product of the s_i and multiply the equation by s^n.
derive: sx satisfies a monic equation over R.
apply_theorem: Since R is integrally closed, sx lies in R.
conclude: So x = (sx)/s lies in S.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let S be the localization of a commutative ring R at a multiplicative subset M and I an ideal of R. The extension of rad(I) to S equals the radical of the extension of I.

drafts.proof_strategy: Write elements with common denominators and clear the denominators in a power relation.
sketch_steps: derive: Elements of IS have the form φ(b)/φ(t) with b in I.
derive: The image of rad(I) lies in rad(IS).
setup: Let z = φ(a)/φ(s) with z^n in IS.
derive: Clearing denominators gives u, t in M with uta^n in I, so uta lies in rad(I).
conclude: Since z = φ(uta)/φ(uts), z lies in the extension of rad(I).

drafts.canonical_statement: The localization of a Noetherian commutative ring at a multiplicative subset is Noetherian.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="submonoid_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="localization_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Every ideal of the localization is generated by the image of its contraction, which is finitely generated.
sketch_steps: setup: Let J be an ideal of S with contraction A.
derive: Every element of J is a unit multiple of the image of an element of A.
apply_theorem: A is finitely generated because R is Noetherian.
conclude: So J is finitely generated.

drafts.canonical_statement: The localization of an Artinian commutative ring at a multiplicative subset is Artinian.

drafts.proof_strategy: Contract a descending chain to R, where it stabilizes, and extend back.
sketch_steps: derive: Each ideal J of S is the extension of its contraction.
setup: Take a descending chain of ideals of S.
apply_theorem: The contracted chain stabilizes because R is Artinian.
conclude: Extending back, the chain in S stabilizes.

drafts.canonical_statement: The localization of a commutative ring R at a multiplicative subset is a flat R-module.

drafts.proof_strategy: Identify tensoring with S with localization and check that localization preserves injections.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: S ⊗ N is naturally isomorphic to the localization of N.
setup: Let g be an injection from N' to N.
derive: If g(y)/s = 0, then ug(y) = 0 for some u in M, so uy = 0 and y/s = 0.
conclude: The localized map is injective, so S is flat.

conclude: With s = ut, sx lies in I.

setup: If IS = S, write 1 = φ(b)/φ(t) with b in I and t in M.
derive: Then ut = ub for some u in M.
conclude: ut lies in I ∩ M.

drafts.proof_strategy: Show that the nonunits of R_p are exactly the elements of pR_p.
sketch_steps: derive: a/s with a outside p has inverse s/a.
derive: So every nonunit lies in pR_p.
derive: pR_p is proper because p does not meet the complement of p.
conclude: pR_p is the set of nonunits, which is the maximal ideal.

drafts.proof_strategy: Zero being a unit forces the zero ring, and φ(1) = φ(0) gives an element of M equal to 0.
sketch_steps: derive: If 0 lies in M, then φ(0) = 0 is a unit, so S = 0.
setup: If S = 0 then φ(1) = φ(0).
derive: There is u in M with u = 0.
conclude: So 0 lies in M.

drafts.canonical_statement: The localization of an integral domain at a multiplicative subset not containing 0 is an integral domain.

drafts.proof_strategy: Clear the denominators and use that elements of M are nonzero.
sketch_steps: derive: S is nonzero because 0 is not in M.
setup: Let (a/s)(b/t) = 0.
derive: There is u in M with uab = 0, and u is nonzero.
conclude: So a = 0 or b = 0.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let p be a prime minimal over an ideal I of a commutative ring. For every x in p there is y outside I with xy in I. This generalizes the case I = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Consider the multiplicative set generated by x and the complement of p, then take a least exponent.
sketch_steps: setup: Let T be the set of products x^n y with y outside p.
contradiction: If T misses I, a prime containing I and missing T lies strictly inside p.
derive: So x^n y_0 lies in I for some y_0 outside p.
construct: Take the least m with x^m y_0 in I, which is at least 1, and put y = x^(m-1) y_0.
conclude: Then y is outside I and xy lies in I.

drafts.canonical_statement: If R is a reduced commutative ring and p is a minimal prime ideal of R, then the localization R_p is a field.

drafts.proof_strategy: The localization has a unique prime, equal to its nilradical, which vanishes by reducedness.
sketch_steps: derive: Primes of R_p correspond to primes inside p, so p R_p is the only prime.
derive: Hence the maximal ideal equals the nilradical of R_p.
derive: R_p is reduced because R is reduced.
conclude: The maximal ideal is zero, so R_p is a field.

sketch_steps: setup: Take generators x_i and write φ(x_i) as a combination with coefficients a_ij in I.
translate: Regard M as an R[X]-module with X acting as φ, so (XE - A)x = 0.
derive: Multiplying by the adjugate gives det(XE - A) x_i = 0 for each i.
derive: So p = det(XE - A) satisfies p(φ) = 0.
derive: The coefficient of X^(n-j) is a sum of j-by-j principal minors of A up to sign, which lies in I^j.
conclude: p has the required form.

drafts.proof_strategy: View M as an R[X]-module and apply Nakayama's lemma to the ideal (X).
sketch_steps: translate: Make M a finitely generated R[X]-module with X acting as f.
derive: Surjectivity of f says (X)M = M.
apply_theorem: Nakayama's lemma gives a = Xq(X) with (1 - a)M = 0.
derive: So the identity equals f composed with q(f).
conclude: If f(y) = 0, then y = q(f)(f(y)) = 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the equational criterion of flatness to lift a basis of M/mM to a basis of M.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The equational criterion expresses any relation among elements of a flat module through a common family.
setup: Suppose the images of x_1, ..., x_n in M/mM are independent and Σ a_i x_i = 0.
derive: Some b_nj is a unit, which expresses a_n through the other a_i.
induction: Substituting yields a relation among n - 1 elements with independent images, so all a_i vanish.
apply_theorem: Lifting a basis of M/mM gives generators by Nakayama's lemma.
conclude: These generators are independent, so M is free.

sketch_steps: derive: The radical of m^n is m and m^n is proper.
setup: Let xy lie in m^n with y outside m.
construct: Write uy + v = 1 with v in m, and raise it to the n-th power to get u'y + v^n = 1.
conclude: Then x = u'xy + v^n x lies in m^n.

This strengthens the existence statement of primary decomposition.

drafts.proof_strategy: Decompose into irreducibles by Noetherian induction, merge and prune components, then compute rad(I : x) from the decomposition.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Noetherian induction writes I as a finite intersection of irreducible ideals.
apply_theorem: Irreducible ideals of a Noetherian ring are primary.
derive: Merging components with equal radical and removing redundant ones gives the minimal form.
derive: For each x, rad(I : x) is the intersection of rad(J) over J not containing x.
derive: If this is prime, it equals some rad(J).
construct: For J in t, choose x in the other components but not in J.
conclude: Then rad(I : x) = rad(J), so the two sets agree.

drafts.proof_strategy: A prime containing a finite intersection contains a component, and minimality forces equality with its radical.
sketch_steps: setup: Let p be minimal over I.
apply_theorem: p contains a finite intersection, so it contains some J in t.
derive: Taking radicals, rad(J) lies in p, and rad(J) is a prime containing I.
conclude: Minimality gives rad(J) = p.

drafts.proof_strategy: In the quotient, stabilize the annihilators of powers of x and intersect (x^n) with (y).
sketch_steps: setup: Pass to R/I, where the zero ideal is irreducible, and let xy = 0 with y nonzero.
apply_theorem: The chain Ann(x^k) stabilizes at some n.
derive: (x^n) ∩ (y) = 0 by comparing annihilators.
derive: Irreducibility of zero and (y) ≠ 0 give (x^n) = 0.
conclude: So x is nilpotent, and I is primary.

drafts.proof_strategy: A maximal annihilator of a nonzero element is prime.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The nonempty set of annihilators of nonzero elements has a maximal element Ann(x_0).
setup: Let ab lie in Ann(x_0) with b outside it.
derive: Ann(b x_0) contains Ann(x_0), hence equals it by maximality.
conclude: a lies in Ann(b x_0) = Ann(x_0), so Ann(x_0) is prime.

sketch_steps: derive: R/Q is nonzero, so it has an associated prime.
setup: Let p = Ann(x̄) = (Q : x) with x outside Q.
derive: Primariness gives (Q : x) inside rad(Q), and Q lies in (Q : x).
derive: Since p is prime and contains Q, it contains rad(Q).
conclude: So p = rad(Q).

drafts.proof_strategy: Identify Rx with R/p, a domain, and split according to whether Rx meets the image of L.
sketch_steps: derive: Injectivity of f preserves annihilators, so Ass(L) lies in Ass(M).
setup: Let p = Ann(x) with x in M, so Rx is isomorphic to R/p.
derive: Every nonzero element of Rx has annihilator p.
case_split: If Rx meets f(L) nontrivially, p lies in Ass(L).
case_split: Otherwise g is injective on Rx, so p lies in Ass(N).
conclude: Hence Ass(M) lies in the union.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring, every prime minimal over Ann(M) is an associated prime of M.

drafts.proof_strategy: Localize at p, find p R_p as an annihilator, and clear denominators using finite generation of p.
sketch_steps: derive: M_p is nonzero because M is finitely generated and p contains Ann(M).
apply_theorem: M_p has an associated prime over the Noetherian ring R_p.
derive: By minimality of p this associated prime is p R_p, so p R_p = Ann(x/1).
construct: Since p is finitely generated, choose t outside p with p x t = 0.
conclude: Then p = Ann(tx).

drafts.canonical_statement: An ideal of a Noetherian commutative ring has only finitely many minimal prime ideals over it.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="comm_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="noetherian_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ideal_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_primes_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use Noetherian induction on ideals with infinitely many minimal primes.
sketch_steps: setup: Take an ideal I maximal among those with infinitely many minimal primes.
derive: I is neither prime nor the unit ideal, so ab lies in I with a, b outside I.
derive: A minimal prime over I contains a or b, and is then minimal over I + (a) or I + (b).
derive: Both larger ideals have finitely many minimal primes.
contradiction: So I has finitely many minimal primes.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every ideal of a Noetherian commutative ring contains a finite product of prime ideals, the empty product being the unit ideal.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use Noetherian induction, splitting an ideal that is not prime with a pair a, b.
sketch_steps: setup: Take an ideal I maximal among those containing no finite product of primes.
derive: I is neither prime nor the unit ideal, so ab lies in I with a, b outside I.
derive: I + (a) and I + (b) contain products of primes A and B.
derive: AB lies in (I + (a))(I + (b)), which lies in I.
contradiction: So I contains a finite product of primes.

drafts.canonical_statement: Let A be a commutative R-algebra and B a commutative A-algebra with compatible R-algebra structure. If A is integral over R and B is integral over A, then B is integral over R. This is the general transitivity behind the special case of the integral closure.
